title: Almost-linear constant-factor LCS approximation
statement: For two explicit strings of total length n over an alphabet of size at most n^2, is there one randomized word-RAM algorithm running in n^(1+o(1)) time that outputs a valid common subsequence of length at least LCS/C with probability at least 2/3, for an absolute C? The alphabet may grow with n, and C must not depend on the running-time slack.

why_it_matters: It asks whether useful subsequence similarity can be computed at almost input-reading cost.
computational: Enumerate short strings over growing alphabets, compute exact LCS by dynamic programming, and test sampled or block-based subsequence constructions.

title: O(gamma)-word encoding from string attractors
statement: A string attractor is a set of positions such that every distinct nonempty substring has some occurrence crossing one of those positions. If gamma(T) is the minimum attractor size of a length-n string over [n], does every such T have a lossless encoding using O(gamma(T) log(n+2)) bits, including metadata? Require uniform computable encoding and decoding but impose no time bound.

why_it_matters: It asks whether the smallest substring witness set also controls the information needed to store the whole string.
computational: Enumerate binary strings through length 20, compute minimum attractors by set cover or SAT, and count distinct strings with each attractor budget.

title: Exact text-to-pattern Hamming distance below the square-root barrier
statement: Given a text of length n and pattern of length m<=n over a polynomial-size integer alphabet, compute the exact Hamming distance at every alignment. Is there a Las Vegas word-RAM algorithm with expected time O(n m^(1/2-epsilon)) for some absolute epsilon>0? Hamming distance counts unequal aligned symbols; no insertions, deletions or approximation are allowed.

why_it_matters: It asks whether the long-standing square-root factor in exact pattern matching can be improved by a fixed power.
computational: Enumerate small texts and patterns, verify convolution identities in exact arithmetic, and benchmark structured high-alphabet cases.

title: Almost-quadratic exact unweighted tree edit distance
statement: For two explicit rooted ordered labeled trees with n vertices in total, can a deterministic word-RAM algorithm compute exact unit-cost tree edit distance in n^(2+o(1)) worst-case time? Allowed edits relabel a vertex, delete a vertex while promoting its ordered children, and the inverse insertion; each costs one.

Use Theta(log(N+2))-bit words and allow polynomial preprocessing; self-referential copy phrases are permitted.

title: Linear-time pattern matching on LZ77 text

Polynomial preprocessing is allowed, occ is the number of returned positions, and all temporary query space counts.

title: Fully functional suffix trees in O(r) total words
statement: For a binary text ending in a unique sentinel, let r be the number of runs in its Burrows-Wheeler transform. Can its complete suffix-tree interface be represented in O(r) total words with polylog(n) worst-case operations, including parent/child/sibling navigation, depths, lowest common ancestors, suffix links, suffix-array and inverse-suffix-array access, and text access? Count all retained text and all auxiliary indexes; no external text oracle is free.

title: Grammar random access in O(g log g) bits

Can it be stored with all auxiliary information in O(g log(g+2)) bits and support any exact character access in O(log(N+2)) worst-case word-RAM time, after preprocessing polynomial in g? Rule forms are terminal 0 or 1, or concatenation of two earlier variables.

title: General-alphabet Hamming oracles with optimal preprocessing
statement: For two strings of lengths n and m over a polynomial-size integer alphabet and a parameter 1<=x<=min(n,m), can a deterministic index use O((nm/x) polylog(n+m)) preprocessing time and words while answering exact substring Hamming-distance queries in O(x) worst-case time? A query gives starts i,j and a valid common length ell and asks for the number of unequal aligned symbols.

title: Near-linear certification of Karp-Rabin fingerprints
statement: Given a string T of length n over {0,...,sigma-1} and a supplied polynomial-size prime p, can one certify in O(n log n) word-RAM time that no two unequal equal-length substrings collide under h(U)=sum_a U[a] sigma^a mod p? A randomized algorithm must always reject a true collision and certify a collision-free input with probability at least 2/3; all substring lengths are included.

title: Optimal top-k document retrieval in compact space

Return up to k documents containing the length-m pattern, sorted by decreasing occurrence count with ties broken by document identifier; occurrences cannot cross document boundaries.

title: Optimal preprocessing exponent for binary jumbled indexing
statement: Determine the minimum preprocessing exponent alpha for a deterministic binary jumbled index using O(n) words and O(1) worst-case queries. A query (u,v) asks whether a contiguous substring has exactly u zeros and v ones; alpha is the infimum a such that for every eta>0 preprocessing O(n^(a+eta)) is possible. In particular, can the current exponent 3/2 be beaten by a fixed positive amount?

statement: Does every connected undirected Cayley graph of a finite group with at least three elements contain a Hamiltonian cycle? For a group Γ and inverse-closed generating set S not containing the identity, the vertices are Γ and edges join g to gs for s∈S.
source_title: Rapaport-Strasser, E., “Hamiltonicity of Cayley graphs”, Open Problem Garden (2008)
locator: Question, with connectivity and order conventions
open_check: Web search "Cayley Hamiltonian conjecture 2026" 2026-11-16 found 2603.08675 proving moderately dense cases and further group-order cases, not all connected Cayley graphs.
why_it_matters: It asks whether algebraic symmetry guarantees a cyclic traversal of every vertex.
computational: Yes: enumerate finite groups and generating sets, then use Hamiltonian-cycle SAT or exact backtracking with group-based symmetry reductions.

title: Switching reconstruction conjecture
statement: Is every finite simple graph on at least five vertices determined up to isomorphism by the multiset of graphs obtained by switching each vertex once? Switching v toggles adjacency between v and every other vertex while leaving all other pairs unchanged.
source_title: Stanley, Richard P., “Switching reconstruction conjecture”, Open Problem Garden (2013)
quote: Every simple graph on five or more vertices
open_check: Searched "switching reconstruction conjecture solved" and the fetched review on 2026-11-16: found Stanley’s proof for orders not divisible by four, leaving n≥8 divisible by four open.
why_it_matters: It tests whether local edge-complement perturbations uniquely fingerprint a graph.
computational: Yes: enumerate graphs on n=8,12,…, canonically encode each one-vertex switching deck, and search for nonisomorphic graphs with equal multisets.

title: Five-cycle double cover conjecture
statement: Does every finite bridgeless graph have five even subgraphs C1,…,C5, allowing empty subgraphs, such that every edge lies in exactly two of them? An even subgraph has even degree at every vertex and may have multiple connected components.
source_title: Celmins, Uldis A., Preissmann, Myriam, “(m,n)-cycle covers”, Open Problem Garden (2007)
locator: First conjecture and definition of binary cycles
open_check: Searched "5-cycle double cover 2026" and the September 2026 fetched review on 2026-11-16: the ordinary cycle double cover result gives eight even subgraphs, leaving five unresolved.
why_it_matters: It asks for a uniform five-layer refinement of the now-resolved ordinary cycle double cover problem.
computational: Yes: assign each edge a two-element subset of {1,…,5}, and require even parity for each colour at each vertex in a SAT or linear-algebra search.

title: Lovász’s Hamiltonian path conjecture
statement: Does every finite connected vertex-transitive graph have a Hamiltonian path, meaning a simple path containing every vertex? Vertex-transitive means that for any two vertices an automorphism sends one to the other.
source_title: Lovasz, Laszlo, “Hamiltonian paths and cycles in vertex transitive graphs”, Open Problem Garden (2007)
quote: Does every connected vertex-transitive graph have a Hamiltonian path?
open_check: Web search "Lovasz Hamiltonian path 2026 open" 2026-11-16 found 2609.38135 and 2606.09742 improving long-cycle bounds without proving a spanning path.
why_it_matters: It asks whether complete local symmetry prevents obstructions to visiting all vertices once.
computational: Yes: enumerate vertex-transitive graphs from permutation groups and test traceability by Hamiltonian-path SAT, preserving exact certificates.

title: Jones’s planar cycle packing conjecture
statement: For every finite planar graph G, is τ_c(G)≤2ν_c(G), where ν_c is the largest number of pairwise vertex-disjoint cycles and τ_c is the smallest number of vertices whose deletion leaves a forest?
source_title: Kloks, Ton, Lee, Chuan-Min, Liu, Jiping, “Jones' conjecture”, Open Problem Garden (2007)
open_check: Web search "Jones conjecture planar 2026" 2026-11-16 found the Halin and based-planar cases but no general theorem, consistent with the fetched literature review.
why_it_matters: It predicts a sharp packing–covering relation for cycles in planar networks.
computational: Yes: enumerate planar graphs and solve feedback vertex set and vertex-disjoint cycle packing as independent integer programs to compare exact optima.

title: Ramsey number R(5,5)
statement: Determine R(5,5). This is the least N such that every 2-colouring of the edges of K_N has a colour-1 copy of K5, or a colour-2 copy of K5.
source_title: Stanisław P. Radziszowski, Small Ramsey Numbers, revision 18 (24 April 2026)
open_check: Web search "Ramsey R(5,5) 2026 exact" 2026-11-16 found only endpoint exclusions and the published range 43–46, not an exact determination.
why_it_matters: It is an unresolved benchmark for exact clique-versus-independent-set computation.
computational: Yes: use one Boolean edge variable per unordered pair, clauses forbidding the two target cliques, isomorphism pruning, and DRAT certificates for unsatisfiable orders.

title: Ramsey number R(K3,K4,D)
statement: Determine R(K3,K4,D). This is the least N such that every 3-colouring of the edges of K_N has a colour-1 copy of K3, or a colour-2 copy of K4, or a colour-3 copy of D. Here D is the diamond K4 with one edge deleted.
source_title: Stanisław P. Radziszowski, Small Ramsey Numbers, revision 18 (24 April 2026)
open_check: Searched the fetched 2026 survey §6.5 on 2026-11-16: it retains the interval 31–40; web searches for small multicolour Ramsey updates found bounds rather than an exact value.
why_it_matters: It is a concrete unresolved multicolour graph-Ramsey threshold close enough to motivate exhaustive search.
computational: Yes: encode three edge colours and forbid colour-specific embeddings of each target; SAT with graph and colour symmetries can improve or close the published interval.

title: Stability version of degeneracy
statement: For every positive integer t, is there c(t) such that every nonempty graph G with no induced K_{t,t} and no induced subdivision of the 1-subdivision of K_t has a vertex v whose neighbourhood contains no independent set larger than c(t)? The 1-subdivision replaces each edge by a two-edge path, and a further subdivision may lengthen these paths.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
open_check: Searched "stability version of degeneracy" and the workshop corrections on 2026-11-16: only the original weaker formulation is solved; the edited formulation is still posed as open.
why_it_matters: It would strengthen degree-style structure theorems to control independent sets inside neighbourhoods.
computational: Yes: enumerate graphs avoiding the two induced configurations and minimize max-independent-neighbourhood obstructions; fixed small t admits exact induced-subdivision searches.

title: χ-boundedness of net-free graphs with tame triangle-free pieces
statement: For every t≥1, does there exist a function f_t such that χ(G)≤f_t(ω(G)) for every net-free graph G whose triangle-free induced subgraphs all have chromatic number at most t? A net is a triangle with one distinct pendant leaf attached to each triangle vertex; net-free means no induced net.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
open_check: Searched "net-free chi-boundedness" and the workshop discussion on 2026-11-16: the bull-free counterpart is proved, but the net-free version remains a question.
why_it_matters: It asks whether controlling triangle-free pieces controls all colouring difficulty in a larger hereditary class.
computational: Yes: enumerate induced-net-free graphs with fixed clique number, compute all relevant induced chromatic numbers by SAT, and seek families with growing χ.

title: Bounded chromatic number of triangle-free sun-free graphs
statement: Is there an absolute C such that every graph containing no triangle and no induced t-sun for any t≥4 has chromatic number at most C? A t-sun is a chordless t-cycle with one distinct pendant leaf attached to each cycle vertex.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)

why_it_matters: It asks for a simple induced structure forced by sufficiently difficult triangle-free colourings.
computational: Yes: generate high-chromatic triangle-free graphs, detect every induced sun exactly, and use SAT to search for sun-free examples.

title: Polynomial treewidth bounds under one chordal exclusion
statement: Fix a chordal graph H and a hereditary class C of graphs with no induced H. If there is a function f with tw(G)≤f(ω(G)) for every G∈C, must there be constants a,d depending on C and H with tw(G)≤a(ω(G)+1)^d for every G∈C? A chordal graph has no induced cycle of length at least four.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
open_check: Searched the workshop subproblem 8(2) and 2026 treewidth/chordal-exclusion updates on 2026-11-16: found special excluded-tree results but no general polynomial-bound theorem.
why_it_matters: It asks whether qualitative structural control automatically gives efficient quantitative bounds.
computational: Yes: compute exact treewidth and clique number on candidate hereditary families; finite obstructions and extremal sequences can test proposed exponents.

title: Linear pathwidth bounds in hereditary classes
statement: If a hereditary graph class C admits any function f such that pw(G)≤f(ω(G)) for all G∈C, must it admit a constant a with pw(G)≤aω(G) for all G∈C? Here pw is pathwidth and ω is clique number.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)

why_it_matters: It seeks a sharp quantitative form of a structural theorem with algorithmic consequences.
computational: Yes: use exact pathwidth algorithms on induced-subgraph closures of candidate graph sequences and compare pw/ω.

title: Multiplicative treewidth partition threshold
statement: Is there an absolute C such that, for all p,q≥1, every graph G with tw(G)≥Cpq has pairwise vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs H1,…,Hm, each with treewidth at least p, such that simultaneously contracting each H_i to one vertex leaves a graph of treewidth at least q? Vertices outside the H_i are retained.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
locator: Problem 11 (David Wood and Kevin Hendrey), PDF page 4
open_check: Searched the workshop problem 11 and its 2025 apex-minor reference on 2026-11-16: the source gives only a much larger polynomial upper bound, not O(pq).
why_it_matters: It asks how large-scale treewidth can be retained while compressing pieces that themselves have large treewidth.
computational: Yes: enumerate connected vertex partitions in small graphs, compute treewidth before and after contraction, and test extremal ratios for p=q=2 or 3.

title: Polynomial vertex-minor Ramsey numbers
statement: Let R_vm(k) be the least n such that every n-vertex graph has an independent k-vertex graph as a vertex-minor. Is R_vm(k) bounded by a polynomial in k, where vertex-minors are obtained by vertex deletions and local complementations, the latter toggling all edges among one vertex’s neighbours?
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)

why_it_matters: It links local graph transformations to Ramsey theory and stabilizer-state resources in quantum networks.
computational: Yes: enumerate local-complementation orbits and vertex deletions on small graphs, using exact binary matrices to determine R_vm(k) and extremal graphs.

title: Hitting maximum independent sets in bounded-rank-width graphs
statement: For each r≥1, does there exist f_r such that every graph G of rank-width at most r has a vertex set of size at most f_r(ω(G)) meeting every maximum independent set of G? Rank-width is the minimum over subcubic leaf decompositions of the largest GF(2) adjacency-matrix rank across an edge cut of the decomposition.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
locator: Problem 13 (Xiying Du and Rose McCarty), PDF page 5
open_check: Searched "rank-width maximum independent sets eta-bounded" and workshop problem 13 on 2026-11-16: found the question but no resolution.
why_it_matters: It asks whether decomposable graphs have small witnesses intersecting all optimal stable sets.
computational: Yes: enumerate bounded-rank-width graphs, list their maximum independent sets, and solve the minimum hitting-set ILP as a function of clique number.

title: Universal connectivity of integer-flow reconfiguration
statement: Does there exist an integer k≥6 such that, for every finite 2-edge-connected graph with a fixed orientation, any two nowhere-zero integer k-flows are joined by a sequence of such flows whose consecutive differences have support equal to a simple cycle? A k-flow conserves signed flow at every vertex and has 1≤|f(e)|≤k−1 on every edge.

locator: Problem 14 (Louis Esperet), unresolved integer version, PDF page 5

why_it_matters: It asks whether locally changing a cyclic circulation can connect the entire bounded-flow space.
computational: Yes: enumerate bounded integer flows on small bridgeless graphs, build the cycle-move graph, and compute its connected components exactly.

title: Infinitely many nontrivial forbidden graphs with no induced-saturated graph
statement: Are there infinitely many pairwise nonisomorphic finite graphs H, each having an edge and a nonedge, for which no finite H-induced-saturated graph exists? Such a graph G would have at least |V(H)| vertices, contain no induced H, and acquire an induced H whenever any one pair’s adjacency is toggled.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)

why_it_matters: It asks whether failure of induced saturation is an isolated phenomenon or an infinite structural obstruction.
computational: Yes: for fixed small H and order n, SAT can simultaneously forbid induced H in G and require it after every possible edge addition or deletion; finite searches guide possible obstruction families.

title: Balanced planar separators made of two geodesics
statement: Does every finite connected planar graph G on n vertices have a vertex separator S that is the union of the vertex sets of two shortest paths in G and such that every component of G−S has at most n/2 vertices? Shortest refers to distance in the original graph.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
open_check: Searched "planar separator two shortest paths 2026" and workshop problem 31 on 2026-11-16: three paths and the weaker two-thirds balance are known, but no half-balanced two-path theorem was found.
why_it_matters: It could sharpen geometric separators used in planar graph algorithms.
computational: Yes: enumerate planar graphs and all shortest paths, test every pair’s deletion for component balance, and certify a smallest counterexample.

title: Brualdi–Quinn Massey strong edge colouring conjecture
statement: For every finite simple bipartite graph G with parts A and B and maximum degrees Δ_A and Δ_B on the two parts, can its edges be partitioned into at most Δ_AΔ_B induced matchings? An induced matching has no edge of G between endpoints of two distinct matching edges.
source_title: Brualdi and Quinn Massey; Open Problem Garden, “Strong edge colouring conjecture” (2013)
open_check: Web search "Brualdi Quinn conjecture 2026 strong edge" 2026-11-16 found 2611.10883 proving fractional and asymptotic versions, while leaving the exact integral bound unresolved.
why_it_matters: It predicts the sharp asymmetric degree bound for interference-free scheduling in bipartite networks.
computational: Yes: enumerate bipartite graphs with fixed part degrees, form the square of the line graph, and test Δ_AΔ_B-colourability by certified SAT.

title: Polynomial weak-diameter two-colourings at bounded treewidth
statement: Do there exist absolute constants C,d>0 such that every finite graph G of treewidth at most k≥1 has a two-colouring of its vertices in which each monochromatic connected component has weak diameter at most Ck^d? Weak diameter is the largest distance in the original graph G between two vertices of the component.
source_title: Julien Codsi (collector), Open Problems for the 2026 Barbados Graph Theory Workshop (2026)
open_check: Searched "weak diameter bounded treewidth polynomial 2026" and workshop problem 28 on 2026-11-16: the stated bound remains k^{O(k)}, and no polynomial improvement was found. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It would give much more efficient quantitative control of network partitions at bounded treewidth.
computational: Yes: enumerate bounded-treewidth graphs and all two-colourings at small orders, compute component weak diameters by shortest paths, and search for extremal growth with k.

title: Polynomial-time cliques beyond the greedy logarithmic barrier
statement: For G sampled from G(n,1/2), does there exist a constant ε>0 and a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that finds a clique of size at least (1+ε)log_2 n with probability tending to one as n tends to infinity?
source_title: Anastasia Kireeva, Low-degree hardness of finding the largest clique in Erdős–Rényi graph (2026)
open_check: Web searches "clique degree O(log n) polynomial 2026" and "clique constant-degree log polynomials 2025 2026" on 2026-11-16 found no resolution; the June 2026 source still describes the logarithmic barrier.
why_it_matters: It asks whether a typical graph optimization problem has a provable gap between efficient and exhaustive search.
computational: Yes: compare greedy and local-search cliques on G(n,1/2) for n=10^3 to 10^5, with exact branch-and-bound baselines for n≤150.

title: Polynomial-time planted clique recovery below the square-root scale
statement: Fix 0<ε<1/2, choose a uniform set S of k=ceil(n^(1/2-ε)) vertices, and add all edges inside S to G(n,1/2). Is there a randomized polynomial-time algorithm that recovers S with probability tending to one, or can such algorithms be ruled out under a standard complexity assumption?

open_check: Web search "planted clique polynomial time 2026 n^{1/2}" on 2026-11-16 found Kunisky–Mao (arXiv:2609.24780), which improves constants at k=Θ(sqrt(n)) and still states the sub-square-root barrier as a conjecture.
why_it_matters: This is a central average-case hardness assumption behind computational lower bounds in network inference.
computational: Yes: benchmark spectral, message-passing and semidefinite methods across k=n^α for α<1/2; enumerate planted sets only for small n.

title: Logarithmic-degree polynomial algorithms for unplanted clique
statement: For every fixed ε,η>0, construct a possibly randomized polynomial map f from the binomial(n,2) edge indicators of G∼G(n,1/2) to R^n, of degree O(log n). Set A={i:f_i≥1}, B={i:1/2<f_i<1}, and C={i∈A:i is adjacent to every other vertex of A}. Require |A\C|+|B|≤ηn and |C|≥(1-ε)log_2 n with high probability, together with E||f||_2²≤γ log n for some constant γ, giving the clique analogue of the robust rounding convention in Wein’s Definition 1.1.
source_title: Anastasia Kireeva, Low-degree hardness of finding the largest clique in Erdős–Rényi graph (2026)
locator: Unplanted setting, final displayed Open Problem (numbered 35 on page); rounding formalized using Wein (2022), Definition 1.1, https://arxiv.org/pdf/2010.06563
open_check: Web searches "clique degree O(log n) polynomial 2026" and "clique constant-degree log polynomials 2025 2026" on 2026-11-16 found no matching construction; the June 2026 source explicitly asks for it.
why_it_matters: It would test whether low-degree polynomials reproduce the performance of the elementary greedy clique algorithm.
computational: Yes: symbolically expand greedy procedures on n≤12 and optimize truncated multilinear maps against exhaustive clique labels.

title: Perfect 1-factorisations of random regular graphs
statement: For every fixed integer d≥3 and even n with dn even, let G be a uniformly random simple d-regular graph on n labelled vertices. Prove that with probability tending to one G admits a partition of its edges into d perfect matchings such that the union of every two matchings is a Hamilton cycle.
source_title: Nicholas Wormald, Models of random regular graphs (1999)
open_check: Web search "perfect 1-factorisation random regular solved" on 2026-11-16 found the November 2026 hitting-time paper arXiv:2611.02128 still reiterating Wormald’s fixed-degree conjecture; no solution was found.
why_it_matters: It asks for a highly coordinated Hamiltonian structure in a typical sparse regular network.
computational: Yes: enumerate d-edge-colourings for random cubic graphs with n≤40 using SAT and check whether every two-colour subgraph is connected.

title: Barely subcritical largest component in preferential attachment without vertex growth
statement: Start from the empty simple graph on n vertices and add each new edge vw with probability proportional to (d_v+α)(d_w+α), among nonedges, for fixed α>0. Let m_c=nα/[2(α+1)] and m=floor(m_c(1-ε)), where ε→0 and ε^3 n→∞. Prove that the largest component has size (C_α+o_P(1))ε^(-2)log(ε^3 n), and determine C_α>0.
source_title: Svante Janson and Lutz Warnke, Preferential attachment without vertex growth: emergence of the giant component (2019; published 2021)

title: Critical component scaling limit in simple fixed-vertex preferential attachment
statement: Start from the empty simple graph on n vertices and add each new edge vw with probability proportional to (d_v+α)(d_w+α), among nonedges, for fixed α>0. For m=floor(m_c(1+λn^(-1/3))) with m_c=nα/[2(α+1)] and fixed λ∈R, prove convergence in distribution of the ordered component-size sequence (n^(-2/3)L_j)_{j≥1}, and identify its limiting law. source_title: Svante Janson and Lutz Warnke, Preferential attachment without vertex growth: emergence of the giant component (2019; published 2021)

title: Barely supercritical second component in fixed-vertex preferential attachment
statement: Start from the empty simple graph on n vertices and add each new edge vw with probability proportional to (d_v+α)(d_w+α), among nonedges, for fixed α>0. title: Connectivity threshold for simple preferential attachment without vertex growth
statement: Start from the empty simple graph on n vertices and add each new edge vw with probability proportional to (d_v+α)(d_w+α), among nonedges, for fixed α>0. statement: Start with n isolated vertices and repeatedly add a nonedge vw with probability proportional to f(d_v)f(d_w), for a given positive function f on the nonnegative integers. title: Deterministic limiting Ising energy barrier on configuration models
statement: Let G_N be a configuration-model graph with i.i.d. degrees from a fixed distribution of finite mean and minimum degree at least 3, conditioned on even total degree. For H_N(σ)=-(J/2)Σ_{ij∈E}σ_iσ_j-(h/2)Σ_iσ_i, with J,h>0 in the regime where all-minus is the unique metastable state, define Γ_N=min_ω max_{σ∈ω}[H_N(σ)-H_N(-1)], where ω ranges over single-spin-flip paths from all-minus to all-plus. Prove that Γ_N/N converges in graph probability to a deterministic γ∈(0,∞).

title: Optimal sublinear-time concentration of discordant edges in the voter model

title: Discordant-edge profile for voter models on nonregular sparse random graphs
statement: Run the rate-one voter model from independent Bernoulli(u) opinions on a configuration-model graph with a nonconstant bounded degree distribution supported on {3,4,...}. title: Hidden convexity of a product of positive quadratics plus a linear term
statement: For positive-definite A,B∈R^{n×n} and nonzero b∈R^n, find an explicit equivalent tractable convex reformulation of min_x (xᵀAx)(xᵀBx)+bᵀx. The quartic need not itself be convex, although the problem is known to be solvable without that assumption.
source_title: A Survey of Hidden Convex Optimization (Yong Xia, 2019)
open_check: Web search "hidden convexity product two positive definite quadratic forms linear term" 2026-11-16: found solvability and conjugate-function work, but no general hidden-convex reformulation of the stated quartic.
why_it_matters: It probes how much tractability can be explained by an underlying convex representation.
computational: Yes: for n=2, eliminate the stationary equations with exact arithmetic and compare with lifted convex formulations.

title: Log-degree polynomial recovery at the planted-clique square-root threshold
statement: Let vertices independently belong to a planted clique with probability k/n, all within-clique edges be present, and other edges be independent Bernoulli(1/2). For k=ε sqrt(n) with fixed ε>0, construct a polynomial f of degree O(log n) in the adjacency entries satisfying E[(f(Y)-1_{1 in clique})²]=o(k/n). The degree constant may depend on ε.
source_title: Computational Complexity of Statistics: New Insights from Low-Degree Polynomials (Alexander S. Wein, 2025)
open_check: Web search "low-degree planted clique upper bounds Wein 2026" 2026-11-16: the survey and a June 2026 problem page still flag matching polynomial upper bounds; no proof of this stated recovery bound was located.
why_it_matters: It would show that low-degree polynomials match known polynomial-time recovery at a sharp scaling.
computational: Yes: form exact moment matrices for n≤8 and degree at most 3 to solve the optimal polynomial-regression problem for clique membership.

title: Quasipolynomial-degree planted-clique recovery polynomials
statement: In the binomial planted-clique model on n vertices with membership probability k/n and background edge probability 1/2, construct a polynomial f of degree O(log² n) with E[(f(Y)-1_{1 in clique})²]=o(k/n) in the statistically identifiable hard regime k≥(2+ε)log₂ n for fixed ε>0. This asks for the mean-square recovery guarantee itself, rather than just an efficiently evaluable thresholded search.
source_title: Computational Complexity of Statistics: New Insights from Low-Degree Polynomials (Alexander S. Wein, 2025)
open_check: Web search "low-degree planted clique upper bounds Wein 2026" 2026-11-16: the survey and a June 2026 problem page still flag matching polynomial upper bounds; no proof of this stated recovery bound was located. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It would align the low-degree model with exhaustive-search recovery in the hard regime.
computational: Yes: count planted-clique subgraph motifs symbolically and calculate their first and second moments to design candidate recovery polynomials.

title: Low-degree strong separation above the sparse-PCA BBP transition
statement: Let Y∈R^{n×N}; under Q its entries are i.i.d. N(0,1), and under P its columns are N(0,I+βxxᵀ), where x_i independently equals ±1/sqrt(k) with probability k/(2n) each and zero otherwise. Assume n/N→γ>0, 1≪k≪n and λ=β/sqrt(γ)>1. Construct a degree-O(log n) polynomial f with |E_P f-E_Q f|/sqrt(max{Var_P f,Var_Q f})→∞.
source_title: Computational Complexity of Statistics: New Insights from Low-Degree Polynomials (Alexander S. Wein, 2025)
open_check: Web search "sparse PCA low-degree upper bound Wein 2026" 2026-11-16: found lower bounds and algorithmic spectral/search bounds, but no matching upper-bound proof in the survey exact separation formulation.
why_it_matters: It would verify that the polynomial framework captures spectral detection above the classical transition.
computational: Yes: evaluate trace polynomials of the sample covariance and symbolically bound their variances under the sparse prior.

title: Low-degree upper bounds tracking subexponential sparse-PCA detection
statement: For the sparse-PCA observation model with N Gaussian samples from covariance I+βxxᵀ, n/N→γ, x_i independently in {0,±1/sqrt(k)} with nonzero probability k/n, take fixed λ=β/sqrt(γ)<1 and k≳sqrt(n). Construct a polynomial of degree Õ(k²/n) strongly separating this law from i.i.d. standard Gaussian samples, where strong separation means that its mean gap dominates both standard deviations.
source_title: Computational Complexity of Statistics: New Insights from Low-Degree Polynomials (Alexander S. Wein, 2025)
open_check: Web search "sparse PCA low-degree upper bound Wein 2026" 2026-11-16: found lower bounds and algorithmic spectral/search bounds, but no matching upper-bound proof in the survey exact separation formulation.
why_it_matters: It tests whether polynomial degree predicts the full statistical-versus-runtime tradeoff.
computational: Yes: enumerate sparse-support motif polynomials for small sample dimensions and compare exact moments with exhaustive sparse-eigenvalue search.

title: The low-degree threshold for refuting dense random-graph colorability
statement: Determine the sharp q(n) threshold for low-degree polynomial refutation of q-colorability in G(n,1/2). In the formal model, seek polynomials f_n of degree polylog(n) with f_n(G)≥1 on every q-colorable graph and E_{G∼G(n,1/2)}[f_n(G)²]=o(1). Close the gap between the known easy regime q≲n^{1/2} and hard regime q≫n^{2/3}, or obtain sharper degree-dependent bounds.
source_title: Computational Complexity of Statistics: New Insights from Low-Degree Polynomials (Alexander S. Wein, 2025)
open_check: Web search "low-degree refuting colorability 2026" 2026-11-16: found the 2023 n^{1/2} versus n^{2/3} gap restated in later sources, with no closing result.
why_it_matters: It would sharpen an algebraic model of average-case certification complexity.
computational: Yes: for small n, enumerate graphs and q-colorability, then solve a quadratic program for the best degree-D polynomial subject to f≥1 on every colorable graph.

title: A general matrix-valued convex Gaussian min–max theorem
statement: Develop a general CGMT-type comparison theorem for convex regularized estimation of B∈R^{p×k} from Y∈R^{n×k} with a shared Gaussian design X∈R^{n×p}. It should handle general convex losses and penalties, transferring risk and distributional analysis to a tractable auxiliary problem as the vector-valued CGMT does when k=1.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "matrix CGMT general 2026" 2026-11-16: found applications and partial multivariate comparisons, but no versatile theorem covering the source general-loss matrix problem.
why_it_matters: It would unify exact asymptotics for multivariate regression and multiclass prediction.
computational: Yes: solve small matrix regression problems and compare empirical risks with candidate Gaussian auxiliary optimization laws.

title: Cavity analysis beyond convex losses and log-concave posteriors
statement: For proportional-dimensional regression y=Xβ*+ε with p/n→κ∈(0,∞), develop checkable conditions under which removing one feature or observation yields stable approximations for nonconvex M-estimators or non-log-concave posteriors. Derive closed fixed-point equations for coordinate distributions and risk, beyond the convex/log-concave cases where existing leave-one-out arguments close.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
locator: Section 4.2, Leave-one-out or cavity method, p. 25
open_check: Web search "leave-one-out nonconvex log-concave posterior 2026" 2026-11-16: found special nonconvex results but no general stable cavity framework resolving the stated extension.
why_it_matters: It could turn heuristic risk predictions for realistic nonconvex learning into rigorous formulas.
computational: Yes: compare full and leave-one-out solutions for small nonconvex penalized regressions, measuring the stability that a proof would need.

title: Interpolation formulas under prior and likelihood mismatch
statement: For high-dimensional Bayesian regression y=Xβ*+ε with p/n→κ>0, extend adaptive interpolation to compute posterior-mean risk when the fitted prior or likelihood differs from the data-generating model. Find usable conditions giving rigorous limiting free-energy and risk formulas without the matched-model identities used by existing general methods.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "interpolation method misspecified regression 2026" 2026-11-16: found restricted mismatch results already acknowledged by the survey, with no general extension.
why_it_matters: It would explain Bayesian prediction under the model errors that arise in practice.
computational: Yes: use low-dimensional numerical posterior integration under mismatched priors and compare it with candidate replica or interpolation formulas.

title: Thin-shell geometry of mismatched high-dimensional regression posteriors
statement: In Gaussian linear regression with p/n→κ∈(0,∞), let β* be a fixed true coefficient vector and fit a posterior using a possibly mismatched prior π. Determine conditions under which the posterior squared distance from β*, with its appropriate dimensional normalization, concentrates around a deterministic radius, and characterize that radius as a function of π, noise and the limiting signal profile.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "misspecified posterior thin shell proportional asymptotics" 2026-11-16: found log-concave and other special-case progress, but no general characterization of the mismatched posterior shell.
why_it_matters: It would give a geometric criterion for choosing priors in regimes where parameter consistency fails.
computational: Yes: compute exact posteriors for modest p with discrete priors, or run controlled posterior simulations and test concentration of normalized radii.

title: Efficient empirical-moment estimation in proportional regression
statement: Observe y=Xβ*+ε with X_ij i.i.d. N(0,1/n), ε_i i.i.d. N(0,σ²), and p/n→κ∈(0,∞). For a fixed integer r≥3 and coefficient sequences with bounded relevant moments, find the optimal estimator and limiting variance for f_r(β*)=p^{-1}sum_{j=1}^p(β*_j)^r, including whether sqrt(n)-consistent asymptotically normal estimation is possible despite inconsistent vector estimation.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "functional estimation proportional asymptotics moments regression coefficients" 2026-11-16: found special functional and causal-estimation results, but no full optimal-variance theory for the source general empirical-moment problem.
why_it_matters: It separates estimating a meaningful aggregate from recovering every regression coefficient.
computational: Yes: simulate Gaussian designs with controlled coefficient histograms and compare Hermite-corrected moment estimators with exact small-dimensional likelihood calculations.

title: Debiasing correlated Gaussian regression with estimated covariance
statement: For y=Xβ*+ε in the proportional regime p/n→κ>0, suppose the rows of X are correlated-feature Gaussian vectors with unknown covariance Σ. Develop coordinatewise debiasing and valid confidence intervals that account for the non-negligible error of a data-driven estimate of Σ, without assuming operator-norm consistent covariance estimation. State conditions broad enough to extend the known-covariance sharp asymptotic theory.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "debiasing unknown covariance proportional 2026" 2026-11-16: found methods under structural or known-covariance assumptions, but no general extension accounting for inconsistent covariance estimation as posed in the survey.
why_it_matters: It would make high-dimensional confidence intervals usable when feature correlations must be learned from the same data.
computational: Yes: simulate dense covariance matrices at p≈n and measure interval coverage after several covariance-estimation and debiasing choices.

title: Exact M-estimator risk under jointly Gaussian dependent designs
statement: Let X=sum_{i=1}^k g_i A_i∈R^{n×p}, with independent g_i∼N(0,1) and known deterministic matrices A_i, and observe y=Xβ*+ε. In proportional dimensions, derive exact asymptotic risks for regularized M-estimators under useful conditions permitting dependence both across rows and across columns, beyond independent-row Gaussian equivalence.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "M-estimators jointly Gaussian arbitrary dependence 2026" 2026-11-16: found general dependent-Gaussian spectral theory, but no general exact-risk theorem for the survey statistical model.
why_it_matters: It could extend sharp learning predictions to spatial and time-series designs.
computational: Yes: choose a small deterministic matrix family A_i modeling temporal dependence and compare convex-regression risk with proposed deterministic equivalents.

title: Comparison inequalities for rotationally invariant designs
statement: Let X=USVᵀ∈R^{n×p}, with U,V independent Haar orthogonal matrices and S a deterministic rectangular singular-value matrix. Develop a natural counterpart of Gaussian min–max comparison inequalities that gives finite-sample or sharp proportional-limit risk guarantees for convex regularized regression under X, without replacing its prescribed singular spectrum by a Gaussian one.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "rotationally invariant Gaussian comparison inequality 2026" 2026-11-16: found AMP and spectral methods, but no general CGMT counterpart for a prescribed rotationally invariant spectrum.
why_it_matters: It would provide a second general route to risk formulas beyond AMP.
computational: Yes: compare random Haar designs with fixed spectra and candidate auxiliary optimization problems in dimensions p≤300.

title: Adaptive interpolation for rotationally invariant regression at general SNR
statement: For y=USVᵀβ*+ε with independent Haar U,V, deterministic singular values S, known product prior for β* and Gaussian noise, prove an adaptive-interpolation formula for Bayes mean-square risk in proportional dimensions across general signal-to-noise ratios. The goal is to remove the high-temperature or low-SNR restrictions of existing general-spectrum results.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
locator: Section 4.5.2, Adaptive Interpolation Method question, p. 29
open_check: Web search "rotationally invariant adaptive interpolation Bayes low SNR 2026" 2026-11-16: found proofs for large subclasses and high-temperature regimes, but no unrestricted general-spectrum general-SNR theorem.
why_it_matters: It would identify information-theoretic limits for structured measurement systems.
computational: Yes: numerically integrate posteriors for small discrete-prior models and compare the risks with candidate scalar variational formulas over a range of spectra.

title: A leave-one-out theory for rotationally invariant M-estimators
statement: For proportional regression y=Xβ*+ε with X=USVᵀ and independent Haar singular vectors, develop a leave-one-out argument yielding entrywise distributions of debiased convex M-estimators. It should explicitly handle the dependence created by deleting a row or column of a rotationally invariant matrix and support confidence intervals for individual coefficients.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "rotationally invariant leave-one-out debiased M-estimators 2026" 2026-11-16: found specialized debiasing and GCV results, but no general cavity method of the requested kind.
why_it_matters: It would turn global spectral risk predictions into valid inference for specific coordinates.
computational: Yes: simulate Haar matrices with fixed spectra and measure the dependence and correction terms induced by feature deletion.

title: Universality of noisy LASSO under semi-random Fourier designs
statement: Let X be a randomly subsampled, suitably randomized p×p Fourier matrix with n/p→δ∈(0,1), and y=Xβ*+ε. Prove conditions under which the noisy LASSO estimator argmin_b {||y-Xb||²/2+λ||b||_1} has the same limiting normalized squared error as a Haar rotationally invariant design with the same singular values. The desired result covers a convex objective without adding a fixed strongly convex penalty.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "LASSO semi-random universality 2026" 2026-11-16: found noiseless LASSO and strongly convex estimator universality, but no general noisy non-strongly-convex theorem closing this survey question.
why_it_matters: It would justify sharp regression predictions for structured sensing rather than ideal Gaussian measurements.
computational: Yes: compare Fourier and Haar designs at matched spectra for sparse signals and estimate the difference in LASSO risk as dimensions grow.

title: Spectral phase-retrieval universality for coded diffraction
statement: Let F_p be the p×p Fourier matrix and X stack the blocks F_pD_1,...,F_pD_L for independent random diagonal masks D_l. Given phase-retrieval observations y_i=|(Xβ*)_i|², prove a sharp asymptotic overlap or risk formula for spectral estimators and determine when it matches a rotationally invariant sensing design with the same singular spectrum.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "coded diffraction spectral universality 2026" 2026-11-16: found orthogonally invariant theory and empirical CDP agreement plus stability results, but no general sharp CDP spectral-universality theorem.
why_it_matters: It would connect phase-retrieval theory to physically implementable Fourier measurements.
computational: Yes: simulate masked Fourier sensing for p≤512, compare spectral overlaps with matched Haar designs, and inspect mask-dependent deviations.

title: Bayes-risk universality for structured sensing designs
statement: For proportional regression y=Xβ*+ε with a specified product prior and Gaussian noise, determine whether the Bayes-optimal risk p^{-1}E||β*-E[β*|X,y]||² is universal between a semi-random structured X, such as subsampled Fourier or coded diffraction designs, and a rotationally invariant design with the same singular values. Identify the required structural and moment conditions or construct a counterexample.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "Bayes optimal structured designs universality 2026" 2026-11-16: found algorithmic universality and special information-theoretic models, but no full structured-design Bayes-risk comparison resolving this question.
why_it_matters: It asks whether singular values alone describe the information available in practical sensing systems.
computational: Yes: use small discrete priors to enumerate exact posterior means for paired structured and Haar sensing ensembles.

title: Posterior contraction for non-intrinsic functional losses
statement: Develop a general posterior-contraction framework for a low-dimensional functional h(θ) in a high-dimensional model P_θ, controlling Π(|h(θ)-h(θ*)|>ε_n|data)→0 at the functional-optimal rate. The theorem should work when global contraction in Hellinger distance yields an inadequate rate for the chosen directional loss, and should supply usable prior and testing conditions beyond target-by-target constructions.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "posterior contraction non-intrinsic losses 2026" 2026-11-16: found sup-norm, operator-norm and posterior-correction special cases, but no general target-optimal functional framework.
why_it_matters: It would support Bayesian uncertainty statements for the scientific quantity of interest rather than an entire model.
computational: Yes: compare exact posteriors under different priors in small high-dimensional Gaussian models to test candidate prior-mass and directional-testing conditions.

title: Adaptive source selection for diffusion-network recovery
statement: An unknown directed network has N vertices and at most d parents per vertex; infections propagate with independent edge transmission times, and each observed cascade records infection times up to a fixed horizon. Suppose some unknown distribution over initial source vertices makes the population-likelihood Hessian satisfy the incoherence and regularity conditions of Theorem 1, which permits recovery from O(d³ log N) passive cascades. Determine conditions and an adaptive source-selection algorithm, without knowing that distribution or the network, that attains this bound or improves its dependence on d.
source_title: Open Problem: Finding Good Cascade Sampling Processes for the Network Inference Problem (Manuel Gomez-Rodriguez, Le Song, Bernhard Schoelkopf, 2014)
quote: Suppose there exists an unknown P(s) where the incoherence conditions hold
open_check: Web search "active cascade incoherence network inference" 2026-11-16: found passive recovery results and the original question, but no resolution of adaptive source selection under the stated unknown-distribution assumption.
why_it_matters: It would turn passive observations of spreading processes into statistically justified experimental interventions.
computational: Yes: enumerate directed graphs of small N, compute or estimate their Fisher information under source distributions, and test adaptive designs.

title: Removing path independence from neural-network spin-glass models
statement: For an H-layer fully connected ReLU network with hinge loss and Λ effective weights constrained by sum_i w_i²=Λ, establish a rigorous connection between its loss landscape and the spherical H-spin Hamiltonian Λ^{-(H-1)/2}sum_{i1,...,iH}Z_{i1,...,iH}w_{i1}⋯w_{iH}. The connection should preserve informative critical-point predictions while removing assumptions that activation indicators are independent of input data and that different paths have independent inputs; alternatively, identify realistic architectures where such a connection holds.
source_title: Open Problem: The landscape of the loss surfaces of multilayer networks (Anna Choromanska, Yann LeCun, Gérard Ben Arous, 2015)
quote: eliminate unrealistic assumptions of variable independence
open_check: Web search "loss surfaces spin-glass independence assumptions open problem" 2026-11-16: later general-activation work still explicitly retains a path-independence assumption, so the requested removal was not found.
why_it_matters: It tests whether spin-glass explanations of optimization describe actual networks rather than an independence surrogate.
computational: Yes: on small networks enumerate activation regions and numerically locate stationary points, then compare their indices and energies with the spin-glass prediction.

title: Fish–Reyzin common-word meeting conjecture
statement: Generate a binary n-state DFA by choosing both outgoing transition targets independently and uniformly for every state. Is there a constant c>0 such that for every fixed pair of states u,v and every λ>0, with probability 1-o(1) over the DFA, a uniform word W of length floor(cn) satisfies Pr_W[δ(u,W)≠δ(v,W)]≤O(n^{-λ})? Prove or disprove the conjecture with the same word driving both trajectories.
source_title: Open Problem: Meeting Times for Learning Random Automata (Benjamin Fish, Lev Reyzin, 2017)
quote: we conjecture that with high probability the meeting time is O(n)
open_check: Web search "random DFA coupled meeting 2026" 2026-11-16: Quattropani–Sau 2023 still states the common-word conjecture as open, while disproving its independent-walk analogue and reporting numerical evidence against such a fast tail.
why_it_matters: It proposes a route from synchronization to faster average-case automaton learning, and its possible failure identifies the limit of that route.
computational: Yes: form the n²-state pair chain with the two shared-letter transitions, and compute exact nonmeeting probabilities through floor(cn) steps.

title: Linear expected synchronization time of random automata
statement: Fix an alphabet size r≥2 and sample an n-state DFA by choosing r distinct ordered transition targets uniformly and independently at each vertex. Let τ_sync be the first length at which an i.i.d. uniform input word sends all n starting states to the same state. Does E[τ_sync|DFA]/n converge in probability to 2 as n→∞?
source_title: On the meeting of random walks on random DFA (Matteo Quattropani and Federico Sau, 2023)
quote: Conjecture 2.7. Using the notation introduced in Conjecture 2.4
open_check: Web search "random DFA synchronization expected time 2n conjecture Quattropani Sau" 2026-11-16: found their 2023 conjecture and independent-coalescence theorem, but no proof for common-word synchronization. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It would quantify the typical cost of erasing unknown initial state information in random finite-state systems.
computational: Yes: for small n solve hitting-time equations on the at most 2^n image subsets under random letters, and compare mean synchronization times divided by n.

title: Sharp proportional-asymptotic generalization for nonlinear in-context learners
statement: Pretrain on n sequences of T labeled examples from k linear regression tasks y=xᵀβ_j+z with x,β_j∈R^p. Derive sharp ID and novel-task OOD prediction-risk formulas for nonlinear attention architectures in the proportional regime n/p²→α, T/p→τ, k/p→κ, with positive finite ratios, and finite-sample error bounds for those formulas. This asks to extend known single-layer linear-attention formulas rather than rederive them.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
open_check: Web search "in-context learning proportional generalization 2026" 2026-11-16: found sharp linear-attention results and finite-sample Bayesian meta-learning bounds, but no general sharp nonlinear-attention extension requested by the survey.
why_it_matters: It would connect pretraining scale and task diversity to measurable prediction error.
computational: Yes: train small attention models on Gaussian regression-task mixtures and test convergence as the three aspect ratios are held fixed.

title: The retrieval–generalization tradeoff in in-context learning
statement: For a learner pretrained on n context sequences of length T from k regression tasks in dimension p, characterize the achievable pair (R_ID,R_OOD) of squared prediction risks on seen tasks and new tasks. Determine how its frontier changes with parameter count, T, k and pretraining duration, including conditions under which improving retrieval must hurt novel-task generalization and conditions allowing simultaneous improvement.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)
quote: Tradeoffs Between ID and OOD ICL
open_check: Web search "in-context learning ID OOD tradeoff training duration 2026" 2026-11-16: found feature-selection models with in-context benign overfitting, but no general frontier characterizing the stated architecture and training dependencies.
why_it_matters: It distinguishes useful task learning from memorization and explains when the two can coexist.
computational: Yes: sweep task diversity and training duration in small regression transformers and plot both risks to locate candidate frontier transitions.

title: Algorithm-dependent pretraining guarantees for in-context learning
statement: For regression-task prompts ((x_1,y_1),...,(x_T,y_T),x_{T+1}) in dimension p, establish ID and new-task risk guarantees for a nonlinear transformer after S specified gradient-based pretraining updates on n sequences from k tasks. The bounds should depend explicitly on S, the optimizer and architecture, rather than assuming an ideal Bayes predictor or weights chosen to implement a regression algorithm.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)

title: Accuracy–certifiability limits of high-dimensional nonconvex unlearning
statement: Let A(D) be a randomized estimator trained on n observations with p/n→κ>0, and let M contain m records to delete. Determine the best achievable retained-data prediction risk and update cost for an unlearner U(A(D),M) whose output law is indistinguishable from A(D\M) at prescribed certification parameters, for nonconvex training objectives. Characterize the dependence on m/n, p/n and the access allowed to retained data.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)

title: Reliable and sample-efficient unlearning audits in high dimensions
statement: Given repeated outputs of an unlearning procedure U(A(D),M) and a retraining reference A(D\M), develop statistically calibrated tests for residual dependence on the m deleted records when the parameter dimension p is comparable to n. Determine audit sample complexity and detection limits as functions of p,n,m and the size of the privacy violation, including efficient tests when full retraining references are unavailable.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)

computational: Yes: simulate matched and deliberately incomplete deletion procedures, varying dimension and replicate count to measure test size and power.

title: Multiple-testing guarantees for adaptively discovered neural circuits
statement: When screening q neurons, heads or circuit hypotheses using activations and interventions on sampled inputs, develop a testing framework that controls a stated familywise error or false-discovery rate at level α despite adaptive circuit selection. Determine sufficient sample sizes and power conditions for validating behavior-specific causal contributions on new inputs.
source_title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Reflections on Progress and Open Problems (Arian Maleki, Subhabrata Sen, Sivaraman Balakrishnan, Verena Zuber, Chao Gao, Rishabh Dudeja, Christos Thrampoulidis, Anru Zhang, Weijie Su, Jason M. Klusowski, Po-Ling Loh, Ali Shojaie, 2026)

title: Uniform-distribution learning of Talagrand DNF formulas
statement: Let m=ceil(log₂ n) and q=ceil((log₂ n)²), with q≤n, and let f on {0,1}^n be an OR of n monotone conjunctions, each containing m of the first q variables. Is there an algorithm using only i.i.d. uniform labeled examples that, for every such f, outputs a hypothesis of error at most ε with probability at least 1-δ in time poly(n,1/ε,log(1/δ))? The source also asks for the easier average-case guarantee when the n terms are drawn independently and uniformly with replacement.
source_title: Learning Talagrand DNF Formulas (Homin K. Lee, 2010)
quote: Does there exist a polynomial-time algorithm for learning the class of Talagrand DNF formulas
open_check: Web search "Talagrand DNF learning polynomial" 2026-11-16: found random-DNF algorithms requiring separated terms and newer testing results, but no learner resolving the overlapping Talagrand construction.
why_it_matters: It isolates a concrete obstacle to learning polynomial-size DNF without membership queries.
computational: Yes: enumerate m-subsets of q variables for modest n, form random formulas, and compare Fourier-based or optimization-based learners on uniform samples.

title: Strong statistical-query lower bounds for Talagrand DNFs
statement: For the class of n-term monotone DNFs whose terms have length ceil(log₂ n) and involve only the first ceil((log₂ n)²) coordinates, prove or rule out a superpolynomial lower bound on strong PAC learning by statistical queries under the uniform input distribution. In particular, determine whether polynomially many queries with inverse-polynomial tolerance can achieve arbitrary requested error ε in polynomial time.
source_title: Learning Talagrand DNF Formulas (Homin K. Lee, 2010)

title: Logarithmic-time constant-regret conditional-probability reductions
statement: For labels y∈{1,...,k}, construct deterministic training and prediction reductions R,R^{-1} to an arbitrary binary squared-loss regression oracle B, both taking O(log k) time. For every distribution D and every B, require E_{(x,y)∼D}[(R^{-1}(x,y)-D(y|x))²]≤C E_{(x′,y′)∼D′}[(B(x′)-E[y′|x′])²] for a universal C, where D′ is the distribution of oracle examples induced by R, sampled uniformly within each example’s oracle calls. Alternatively prove that no such reduction exists.

computational: Yes: encode small deterministic reduction trees and adversarial oracle outputs as polynomial inequalities, then use exact optimization to search for unavoidable regret amplification.

title: Consistent learning of 2-CNF under arbitrary missing information
statement: An example x∈{0,1}^n is drawn from any distribution D and labeled by an unknown 2-CNF f; an arbitrary example-dependent masking process replaces any coordinates by *, while leaving its label visible. Is there a learner running in poly(n,size(f),1/ε,1/δ) time that outputs a Boolean hypothesis h with probability at least 1-δ and conflict probability at most ε? On a partial input h abstains exactly when its values over all consistent completions differ, and a conflict means that h has a definite prediction opposite to the observed label.
source_title: Missing Information Impediments to Learnability (Loizos Michael, 2011)

title: Existence of one-way functions
statement: Does there exist a polynomial-time computable family f_n:{0,1}^n→{0,1}^{poly(n)} such that, for every probabilistic polynomial-time A, Pr[f_n(A(f_n(x)))=f_n(x)] is negligible in n for uniform x? The adversary may return any preimage, not necessarily x.

title: Classical polynomial-time integer factorization

title: Existence of NPT bound entanglement
statement: Does there exist a finite-dimensional bipartite density matrix ρ whose partial transpose has a negative eigenvalue but from which no positive asymptotic rate of singlets can be distilled by local operations and classical communication, even using arbitrarily many copies? Equivalently, must every NPT state be distillable?

title: Closed formula for two-qubit relative entropy of entanglement
statement: For every density matrix ρ on C²⊗C², find a closed expression for E_R(ρ)=min_{σ separable} Tr[ρ(log ρ−log σ)]. In this dimension separability can equivalently be replaced by positivity of the partial transpose.

title: Circuit complexity of repeated known-state preparation
statement: For a known m-qubit pure state |ψ⟩, characterize the asymptotic minimum circuit cost C(|ψ⟩^{⊗n}) in terms of n,m and C(|ψ⟩). Use the source gate model of rotations exp(iφσ_u), with σ_u a Pauli string and cost |φ|, and start each preparation from an all-zero state.

title: Lockability of two-way distillable entanglement
statement: Can discarding one qubit A′ from Alice cause an unbounded decrease D_↔(AA′:B)_ρ−D_↔(A:B)_{Tr_A′ρ} as the remaining local dimensions grow? Here D_↔ is the asymptotic singlet-distillation rate under local operations and unlimited two-way classical communication.

title: Lockability of distillable secret key
statement: Can discarding one qubit A′ held by an honest party cause K_D(AA′:B)_ρ−K_D(A:B)_{Tr_A′ρ} to grow without bound with the other local dimensions? K_D is the asymptotic secret-bit rate under local quantum operations and public classical communication with Eve holding a purification.

title: Polynomial entanglement lower bounds for robust f-routing
statement: For some fixed 0<ε<0.1, exhibit an explicit family f_n:{0,1}^n×{0,1}^n→{0,1} such that every simultaneous one-round routing protocol requires log₂ of the shared pure state’s local dimension at least n^c for some constant c>0. Alice initially holds an unknown qubit and x, Bob holds y, and the qubit must end at Alice for f_n=0 and Bob for f_n=1, with diamond-norm error at most ε on every input; local operations and message dimensions are unrestricted.

title: Information-theoretically sound classical verification of BQP
statement: Does every language L in BQP admit a polynomial-round classical interactive protocol with a probabilistic polynomial-time verifier and an honest polynomial-time quantum prover, with completeness at least 2/3 and soundness at most 1/3 against every computationally unbounded cheating prover? Only one prover and entirely classical communication are allowed.

title: Constant trace-distance separability testing
statement: For fixed constant 0<ε<1, determine the time complexity in d of distinguishing a separable ρ on C^d⊗C^d from a state with inf_{σ separable}(1/2)||ρ−σ||₁≥ε, given all d⁴ matrix entries and the promise that one case holds. In particular, is d^{O(log d)} time sufficient in trace distance?

title: Absolute separability versus absolute PPT
statement: For all local dimensions m,n≥3, is a density matrix ρ on C^m⊗C^n separable after every global unitary conjugation whenever (UρU†)^{T_B} is positive semidefinite for every global unitary U? More generally, characterize the eigenvalue lists for which every state with those eigenvalues is separable.

title: Maximum number of mutually unbiased bases in composite dimensions
statement: Determine M(d), the maximum number of orthonormal bases B₁,…,B_M of C^d satisfying |⟨b_{ri},b_{sj}⟩|²=1/d for every r≠s and every i,j, when d is not a prime power. The dimension-six case is excluded here because it has a reported solution; dimensions such as d=10 remain part of the question.

title: Existence of an AME state of eight ququarts
statement: Does there exist a pure state |ψ⟩∈(C⁴)^{⊗8} whose reduced density matrix on every set S of four parties is I_{4⁴}/4⁴? This is an AME(8,4) state, equivalently a pure quantum code with parameters ((8,1,5))₄.

statement: For an n-bit replicated database, construct a two-server private information retrieval protocol with total communication (log n)^{O(1)} bits, perfect or statistical privacy against either noncolluding server, and correctness probability at least 2/3 for every requested bit. No computational hardness assumption may be used.

The evaluator must support all polynomial-size Boolean circuits with ciphertext size and decryption cost bounded polynomially in security parameter, independently of the evaluated circuit size.

The public key and decryption complexity must be independent of the chosen evaluation depth, so leveled schemes alone do not meet the goal.

statement: Construct a succinct noninteractive argument for every NP relation from a standard falsifiable cryptographic assumption such as LWE, in a common-reference-string model. title: Optimal field size for constant-locality maximally recoverable codes

Such a code has dimension n−an/r−h and corrects every erasure pattern that becomes at most a erasures per group after deleting at most h erased positions; determine in which regimes superlinear q is necessary.

A pattern is correctable if some choice of these component codes makes restriction to unerased coordinates injective.

open_check: Web searches for 'higher order MDS 2026 explicit field size', 'maximally recoverable 2026 constant locality field size', and 'grid codes correctable 2026 polynomial' on 2026-11-16 found parameter-specific improvements, not resolutions of these general questions; the fetched 2026 survey explicitly lists this question in its conclusion.

title: Optimal alphabet size of higher-order MDS codes
statement: For k=Θ(n) and order m≥3, determine the minimum field size q of an [n,k] code C such that P_m⊗C is maximally recoverable, where P_m={x∈F_q^m:Σ_i x_i=0}. Here maximal recoverability means correcting every erasure pattern correctable by some tensor code of these component dimensions; current general field bounds have exponential dependence with a gap in their dependence on m.
source_title: Maximal Recoverability: A Nexus of Coding Theory (Joshua Brakensiek and Venkatesan Guruswami, 2026)

statement: Construct deterministic explicit [n,k] higher-order MDS(m) codes for k=Θ(n), m≥3, over fields q=exp(poly(m)n), with construction time polynomial in the output bit length. Higher-order MDS(m) means that tensoring the code with the length-m single-parity-check code corrects every erasure pattern permitted by the tensor topology; known existential fields are singly exponential while the survey’s explicit constructions are doubly exponential in n.
