open_check: Web search '24 0 10 quantum code existence' on 2026-11-16 found no construction or nonexistence proof for the pure 24-qubit case; the fetched source explicitly poses it and gives the forced weight distribution.
why_it_matters: It is an extremal test of how broadly a many-qubit state can distribute its entanglement.
computational: Yes; search self-dual additive length-24 codes over F₄ as a stabilizer subcase, checking all low-weight words, or optimize symmetry-restricted state tensors.

title: Seven qubits protecting a qutrit: a ((7,3,3))₂ code
statement: Does there exist a three-dimensional subspace Q⊆(C²)^{⊗7} with orthogonal projector P satisfying PEP=λ_E P for every seven-qubit Pauli operator E of weight at most two? Such a code would exactly correct an arbitrary error on any one qubit, without assuming stabilizer or codeword-stabilized structure.
source_title: QECC-733 (NumQI research-software documentation; Cao et al. VarQEC problem, 2022)
open_check: Web search '((7,3,3)) quantum solved 2026' on 2026-11-16 found numerical nonexistence evidence and a CWS-only exclusion, not a general impossibility proof; the fetched NumQI page explicitly marks the general question open.
why_it_matters: It asks whether a genuinely nonadditive code can outperform the seven-qubit stabilizer benchmark in logical dimension.
computational: Yes; optimize three orthonormal 128-component code vectors, then use exact Knill–Laflamme polynomial constraints or sum-of-squares certificates.

title: One-shot resources for implementing Gibbs-preserving quantum maps
statement: For a finite Hamiltonian H and inverse temperature β, characterize the minimum work and time-coherence resources needed to implement a given completely positive trace-preserving map Φ with Φ(e^{−βH}/Tr(e^{−βH}))=e^{−βH}/Tr(e^{−βH}), within diamond-norm error ε. Free operations append Gibbs ancillas, apply a total-energy-preserving unitary, and discard ancillas; additional batteries and coherent reference states are consumed resources whose costs must be quantified.
source_title: Thermodynamic implementation of Gibbs-Preserving Maps (Philippe Faist, Open Quantum Problems, 2023)
locator: Problem 46, Problem and Accounting for coherence and work resources
open_check: Web search 'Gibbs-preserving implementation 2026 resources open' on 2026-11-16 found no complete one-shot implementation-cost characterization; the fetched OQP page lists solved trivial-Hamiltonian and time-covariant subcases separately.
why_it_matters: It measures the physical resource cost of quantum processes treated as free in an abstract thermodynamic model.
computational: Yes; optimize small-dimensional Stinespring dilations and energy-preserving unitaries with explicit finite batteries and reference clocks.

title: Cutoff for constant-rate zero-range processes on higher-dimensional tori
statement: For fixed d ≥ 2 and density ρ > 0, put m particles on the N vertices of (Z/LZ)^d with m/N → ρ. Each occupied vertex sends one particle at total rate 1 to a uniformly chosen neighbor; prove total-variation cutoff as L → ∞, meaning t_mix(ε)/t_mix(1−ε) → 1 for every fixed 0 < ε < 1/2.
source_title: Modern aspects of Markov chains: entropy, curvature and the cutoff phenomenon — Justin Salez (2025)
open_check: Web search "zero-range cutoff lattices" 2026-11-16 found mean-field results but no lattice solution; Salez (2025) explicitly poses Problem 2.6, while the attempted arXiv API query returned HTTP 429. 2026-11-16: arXiv title search (ti:cutoff AND ti:constant AND ti:rate AND ti:zero AND ti:range AND ti:processes) returned 1 result(s), none claiming a resolution.
why_it_matters: This would extend sharp equilibration beyond the currently tractable mean-field geometry.
computational: Simulate conservative particle dynamics at several L and fixed density, or diagonalize the generator for small particle numbers.

title: Ising Glauber cutoff throughout the tree-uniqueness regime
statement: For each fixed maximum degree Δ ≥ 3 and inverse temperature 0 ≤ β < atanh(1/(Δ−1)), prove total-variation cutoff for single-site heat-bath dynamics of the zero-field ferromagnetic Ising distribution μ(σ) proportional to exp(β sum_{uv∈E} σ_u σ_v) along every growing sequence of graphs of maximum degree Δ. This is the concrete tree-uniqueness case of the source’s question about the full rapidly mixing regime.
source_title: Modern aspects of Markov chains: entropy, curvature and the cutoff phenomenon — Justin Salez (2025)
open_check: Web search "cutoff Ising uniqueness 2026" 2026-11-16 found high-temperature information-percolation and curvature results but no theorem covering the entire tree-uniqueness interval; the 2025 source lists the broader problem as open.
why_it_matters: Rapid sampling bounds would become sharp stopping rules throughout the uniqueness phase.
computational: Enumerate 2^n spin configurations on small bounded-degree graphs and compare simulated mixing windows over larger graph families.

title: Polynomial mixing for the planar Ising model with plus boundary
statement: For each fixed inverse temperature β > 0, prove that single-site heat-bath Glauber dynamics for the nearest-neighbor ferromagnetic Ising model on an L × L square, with every boundary spin fixed to +1, has t_mix(1/4) ≤ L^C(β). Time here counts individual vertex updates; the open issue is polynomial rather than quasi-polynomial dependence on L at low temperature.
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web search "Ising plus boundary polynomial mixing" 2026-11-16 found quasi-polynomial upper bounds and low-temperature random-initialization results, but no all-temperature polynomial bound for this boundary-value problem.
why_it_matters: This is a basic test of whether a favorable boundary removes exponentially slow phase coexistence.
computational: Simulate interface erosion from the all-minus interior for growing L; compute exact gaps on narrow strips.

title: Monotonicity of the ferromagnetic Ising spectral gap in each coupling
statement: Let μ_J(σ) be proportional to exp(sum_{uv∈E} J_uv σ_u σ_v) on a fixed finite graph, with J_uv ≥ 0 and zero external field. Is the spectral gap of continuous-time rate-one-per-vertex heat-bath dynamics nonincreasing in each J_uv? This includes decreasing the temperature and adding ferromagnetic edges.
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web searches "Ising spectral gap interaction strengths monotone" and "Ising spectral gap monotonicity conjecture solved" 2026-11-16 found proofs for cycles and the mean-field model, but no general-graph resolution. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It would turn physical expectations about stronger interactions into a general comparison principle for MCMC.

title: Monotonicity of Ising pairwise total-variation distance in couplings
statement: For the zero-field ferromagnetic Ising heat-bath chain on a fixed graph, let dbar_J(t) = max_{σ,η} ||P_t^J(σ,·)−P_t^J(η,·)||_TV, with every vertex updating at rate one. For each fixed t ≥ 0, is dbar_J(t) nondecreasing in every nonnegative coupling J_uv?
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web search "Ising total variation monotonicity coupling strengths conjecture" 2026-11-16 found coupling and spectral-gap monotonicity papers but no proof of this stronger fixed-time distance statement.
why_it_matters: This would compare entire convergence curves rather than only their asymptotic rates.
computational: For n ≤ 6, exponentiate heat-bath generators and optimize the pairwise total-variation distance as a selected edge coupling varies.

title: Constant-factor comparison of systematic and random Ising scans
statement: For zero-field ferromagnetic Ising dynamics on n vertices, let P be one uniformly random single-site heat-bath update and P_α one complete deterministic sweep in an arbitrary vertex order α. Do universal constants c,C > 0 satisfy c t_mix(P)/log n ≤ n t_mix(P_α) ≤ C t_mix(P), with all mixing times taken at total-variation tolerance 1/4?
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)

computational: Enumerate vertex orders on n ≤ 7 and compare mixing curves of the 2^n-state sweep and random-update kernels.

title: Equivalence of optimal relaxation and mixing for transitive Ising systems
statement: For zero-field ferromagnetic Ising heat-bath dynamics on growing vertex-transitive graphs with n vertices, using one random vertex update per step, is t_rel = Θ(n) equivalent to t_mix(1/4) = Θ(n log n), allowing the inverse temperature to vary with n? Prove the equivalence or give a transitive counterexample.
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web search "Glauber transitive relaxation if and only if" 2026-11-16 found the textbook question and results for particular geometries, but no general transitive-graph equivalence.

title: Optimal n log n mixing for colorings near the maximum-degree threshold
statement: Fix Δ and an integer q > Δ+2. Does the single-vertex heat-bath chain for uniform proper q-colorings of every n-vertex graph of maximum degree at most Δ satisfy t_mix(1/4) = O_Δ,q(n log n)? The bound is to hold uniformly over graphs and initial proper colorings.
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web search "proper colorings Delta+2 mixing 2026" 2026-11-16 found improvements above a multiplicative degree threshold, including the November 2026 claim at (1+1/e+γ)Δ, but no result down to this additive threshold.

title: Degree-times-diameter-squared bound for transitive random-walk mixing
statement: For every finite connected vertex-transitive graph G of degree Δ and diameter D, is the total-variation mixing time of lazy simple random walk at most C Δ D² for a universal C? The walk stays put with probability 1/2 and otherwise chooses a neighbor uniformly.
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web search "transitive mixing diameter degree conjecture 2026" 2026-11-16 found relaxation-time and structural diameter bounds but no universal C Δ D² total-variation mixing theorem.

computational: Enumerate small vertex-transitive graphs and compute mixing times and ratios t_mix/(ΔD²).

title: Mixing-time comparison of bounded-block and single-site Potts dynamics
statement: For the ferromagnetic q-state Potts model on finite graphs, compare single-site heat-bath dynamics with heat-bath dynamics that selects from a cover of blocks of uniformly bounded size. Assuming each vertex has block-selection frequency comparable to 1/n, must their worst-case total-variation mixing times be within constant factors depending only on q, the block-size bound and these frequency bounds?
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web search "Potts block dynamics single-site comparable mixing" 2026-11-16 found relaxation-time comparisons and entropy-factorization bounds but no general worst-case mixing-time comparability theorem; the source explicitly retains the Potts case as open.

title: Possible coalescence numbers of a finite Markov chain
statement: Given an irreducible stochastic matrix P on a finite set S, characterize K(P) = {k(μ): μ is a probability law on functions f:S→S with μ[f(i)=j]=P_ij}. Here k(μ) is the almost-sure number of eventual coalescence classes among the trajectories X_t^i = F_t∘⋯∘F_1(i), where the F_t are independent with law μ.
source_title: Coalescence in Markov Chains — Geoffrey Grimmett and Mark Holmes (2026)
open_check: Web search "coalescence determine K(P)" 2026-11-16 found Grimmett–Holmes and their earlier work but no subsequent general characterization; the May 2026 published article retains Question 3.3. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It identifies which grand couplings can support perfect simulation and which permit persistent avoidance.
computational: For |S|=3 or 4 enumerate supports among the |S|^|S| maps, solve their marginal-feasibility linear programs and compute minimum semigroup ranks.

title: Almost-sure coalescence for every coupling of a random stochastic matrix
statement: Fix n and draw independent q_ij uniformly from (0,1), then put P_ij=q_ij/sum_j q_ij. Is it true with probability one over P that every random-map grand coupling consistent with P has exactly one eventual coalescence class, equivalently K(P)={1}?
source_title: Coalescence in Markov Chains — Geoffrey Grimmett and Mark Holmes (2026)
open_check: Web search "coalescence almost every transition matrix" 2026-11-16 found no resolution; the published 2026 source explicitly lists this as Open problem 3.8.

status_note: Same problem as CN0519 (same source and problem number); kept there.

title: Volume of stochastic matrices representable by a prescribed set of maps
statement: Let S={1,…,n}, let G be a specified subset of the maps S→S, and let P(G) be the irreducible stochastic matrices expressible as convex combinations of the deterministic transition matrices of maps in G. Determine Q(P(G)), where Q is the law obtained by normalizing each row of an n×n matrix of independent Uniform(0,1) entries.
source_title: Coalescence in Markov Chains — Geoffrey Grimmett and Mark Holmes (2026)
open_check: Web search "grand couplings support measure Grimmett" 2026-11-16 found no general volume formula; the May 2026 source gives special cases and leaves Question 7.4 open.

status_note: Same problem as CN0521 (same source and problem number); kept there.

title: Aldous–Caputo spectral-gap conjecture for hypergraph block shuffles
statement: Give each subset A of an n-element vertex set a nonnegative rate α_A, and at that rate uniformly reshuffle the labels occupying A. Assuming the induced one-particle walk is irreducible, is the spectral gap of this permutation chain equal to that of the one-particle walk with jump rates q_xy = sum_{A containing x,y} α_A/|A| for x ≠ y?
source_title: Entropy inequalities for random walks and permutations — Alexandre Bristiel and Pietro Caputo (2024)
open_check: Web search "Caputo hypergraphs spectral gap conjecture solved" 2026-11-16 found Alon–Kozma–Puder’s partial hypergraph theorem and subsequent references still describing the general conjecture as open.

title: Oliveira’s comparison of exclusion mixing with independent particles
statement: On any finite connected weighted graph, let EX(k) be the k-particle symmetric exclusion process and RW(k) the product of k independent random walks with the same edge rates. For 1 ≤ k ≤ n/2, is t_mix^EX(k)(ε) ≤ C t_mix^RW(k)(ε) with a universal constant C, uniformly over graphs, rates and 0 < ε < 1/4?
source_title: The exclusion process mixes (almost) faster than independent particles — Jonathan Hermon and Richard Pymar (2020)
open_check: Web search "exclusion Oliveira conjecture 2026 mixing" 2026-11-16 found recent partial mixing comparisons and the October 2026 Specht-module paper, but no general independent-particle comparison; Hermon–Pymar state the problem explicitly.
why_it_matters: It would formalize the idea that negative dependence cannot greatly slow equilibration.
computational: On graphs with n ≤ 12 construct the binomial(n,k)-state exclusion kernel and product-walk kernel for k=2,3, and compare mixing times.

title: Weak monotonicity of exclusion mixing in the particle number
statement: For every connected weighted n-vertex graph, do universal constants give t_mix^EX(k1)(1/4) ≤ C t_mix^EX(k2)(1/4) whenever 1 ≤ k1 ≤ k2 ≤ n/2? Each process uses the same symmetric edge rates, and its stationary law is uniform on subsets of its particle number.
source_title: The exclusion process mixes (almost) faster than independent particles — Jonathan Hermon and Richard Pymar (2020)
open_check: Web search "exclusion weak monotonicity mixing" 2026-11-16 found the original conjecture and partial results but no all-graph proof or counterexample.
why_it_matters: It would let bounds for a dense exclusion process control every sparser version.
computational: Enumerate small connected weighted graphs and calculate exclusion mixing times for every k ≤ n/2.

title: A profile lower bound comparing labelled interchange and independent walks
statement: Does there exist a universal C > 1 and a continuous nondecreasing function f:[0,1]→[0,1], with f(0)=0 and f(u)>0 for u>0, such that d_IP(k),x(t) ≥ f(d_RW(k),x(Ct)) on every weighted graph, for every k and every distinct labelled starting tuple x? Here IP(k) tracks k marked labels of the interchange process, RW(k) tracks independent walkers from the same tuple, and d denotes total-variation distance from the relevant stationary law.
source_title: The exclusion process mixes (almost) faster than independent particles — Jonathan Hermon and Richard Pymar (2020)
open_check: Web search "exclusion Question 1.12 Hermon" 2026-11-16 found later references to this strengthened comparison but no resolution of the labelled profile inequality.
why_it_matters: A comparison of full distance curves would be stronger than worst-case mixing-time estimates.

title: A profile lower bound comparing exclusion and unlabelled independent walkers
statement: Is there a universal C > 1 and a continuous nondecreasing f:[0,1]→[0,1], with f(0)=0 and f(u)>0 for u>0, such that d_EX(k),A(t) ≥ f(d_RWunlabelled(k),A(Ct)) for every weighted graph, k ≤ n/2 and k-element starting set A? The second process consists of k independent walkers with their labels forgotten and can have multiple particles at a vertex.
source_title: The exclusion process mixes (almost) faster than independent particles — Jonathan Hermon and Richard Pymar (2020)
open_check: Web search "exclusion Question 1.12 Hermon" 2026-11-16 found the original question and subsequent citations, but no proof of the unlabelled profile comparison.

title: Interchange mixing controlled by the slowest exclusion projection
statement: Is there a universal C > 1 and a continuous nondecreasing f:[0,1]→[0,1], positive on (0,1] with f(0)=0, such that t_mix^IP(n)(f(ε)) ≤ C max_{1≤k≤n−1} t_mix^EX(k)(ε) for every finite connected weighted graph and 0 < ε < 1/4? The interchange process permutes all labels, while EX(k) forgets all but membership in a k-element label set.
source_title: The exclusion process mixes (almost) faster than independent particles — Jonathan Hermon and Richard Pymar (2020)
open_check: Web search "exclusion Question 1.12 Hermon" 2026-11-16 found no general theorem reconstructing interchange mixing from the exclusion projections; the source explicitly asks this inequality.

title: Two-thirds spectral comparison under dominance of partitions
statement: For nontrivial partitions σ,τ of n with σ dominating τ, prove λ_min(L(G,τ)) ≥ (2/3)λ_min(L(G,σ)) for every nonnegatively weighted graph G. Here L(G,ρ)=sum_{i<j} w_ij(I−ρ((ij))) in the irreducible representation indexed by ρ; the factor 2/3 is conjectured to be sharp.
source_title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process — Gil Alon (2026)

title: Oliveira’s relaxation-times-log-n bound for the interchange process
statement: For the continuous-time interchange process on any connected weighted graph with n vertices and one-particle spectral gap γ, prove t_mix(1/4) ≤ C γ^−1 log n with a universal C. Every edge {i,j} exchanges its two labels at its prescribed nonnegative rate w_ij.
source_title: Spectral comparison on Specht modules and mixing of the interchange process — Gil Alon (2026)

title: Linear inverse modified log-Sobolev constant for matching Glauber dynamics
statement: Fix λ > 0 and let μ(M) be proportional to λ^|M| on the matchings of any simple graph with m edges. For the discrete-time chain that selects one edge uniformly and heat-bath updates its occupation, prove that the modified log-Sobolev constant is at least c(λ)/m, uniformly over graphs and degrees; equivalently the continuous-time generator P−I contracts relative entropy at rate Ω_λ(1/m).
source_title: Sampling Matchings in Near-linear Time — Tianshun Miao and Yitong Yin (2026)

title: RNC sampling of the monomer–dimer model on unbounded-degree graphs
statement: For every fixed λ > 0, design a randomized parallel algorithm that samples a matching with law within total-variation error n^−c of μ(M) proportional to λ^|M| on any n-vertex simple graph. Require polylogarithmic parallel depth and polynomial total work, with no maximum-degree restriction and for every fixed accuracy exponent c > 0.

title: Near-linear exact sampling of matchings without a degree bound
statement: For every fixed λ > 0, generate an exact sample from μ_G,λ(M) proportional to λ^|M| on any simple n-vertex, m-edge graph in expected Otilde_λ(n+m) time, with no degree restriction. The target is exact distributional correctness rather than a small total-variation error.

title: Subquadratic approximate counting of matchings on sparse graphs
statement: For fixed λ > 0 and a fixed constant relative error ε ∈ (0,1), can Z_G(λ)=sum_{M matching} λ^|M| be approximated with success probability at least 3/4 in Otilde_λ(n^(2−δ)) work for some universal δ > 0, on every graph with m=Θ(n)? More generally seek a polynomial saving over the mn annealing work across all graph densities, beyond input-reading cost.
source_title: Sampling Matchings in Near-linear Time — Tianshun Miao and Yitong Yin (2026)

title: Deterministic FPTAS for the monomer–dimer model at unbounded degree
statement: For each fixed λ > 0, approximate Z_G(λ)=sum_{M matching} λ^|M| within relative error ε by a deterministic algorithm polynomial in n and 1/ε for arbitrary simple n-vertex graphs. The polynomial exponent must be independent of the maximum degree.

title: Rapid mixing of SK Glauber dynamics below beta one with arbitrary fields
statement: Let W be an n×n GOE matrix with off-diagonal variance 1/n, and μ_β,h(σ) proportional to exp((β/2)σᵀWσ+hᵀσ) on {−1,+1}^n. For every fixed 0 ≤ β < 1, does single-site heat-bath Glauber dynamics have polynomial worst-case mixing time with high probability over W, uniformly over arbitrary deterministic external fields h?
source_title: Randomstrasse101: Open Problems of 2024 — Afonso Bandeira and collaborators (2025)

statement: Let μ be uniform on S_n and let α_A ≥ 0 weight subsets A⊆[n] with |A|≥2 and γ(α)=min_i sum_{A containing i} α_A>0. title: Deterministic approximate counting at the tree-uniqueness threshold
statement: For fixed Δ≥3, is there a deterministic fully polynomial approximation scheme for the critical hard-core partition function Z_G(λ_c)=sum_{I independent} λ_c^|I| on graphs of maximum degree Δ, where λ_c=(Δ−1)^(Δ−1)/(Δ−2)^Δ? The algorithm must return relative error at most ε in time polynomial in n and 1/ε, including the critical point itself.
source_title: Rapid Mixing at the Uniqueness Threshold — Xiaoyu Chen, Zongchen Chen, Yitong Yin and Xinyuan Zhang (2024; revised 2026)
locator: §5, concluding open problems, third bullet, p. 53

title: FPRAS for counting colorings with maximum degree plus one colors
statement: For each fixed Δ≥3 and q≥Δ+1, give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for the number Z_q(G) of proper q-colorings of every n-vertex graph of maximum degree Δ. The algorithm should return a relative ε-approximation with probability at least 3/4 in time polynomial in n and 1/ε.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)

title: Odd-color hardness below the maximum-degree threshold
statement: For each fixed odd integer q≥3 and integer Δ>q, prove that approximating the number of proper q-colorings of graphs of maximum degree Δ admits no FPRAS unless NP=RP. The source’s conjecture is known for even q; the unresolved issue is eliminating that parity restriction.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)

title: Approximate edge-coloring counting threshold between degree and twice degree
statement: Identify the constant c∈[1,2], if a constant threshold exists asymptotically as d→∞, separating efficient approximation of the number of proper q-edge-colorings of maximum-degree-d graphs from computational hardness at q=(c+o(1))d. Present sampling/counting algorithms above the threshold and a matching conditional hardness result below it.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)
open_check: Web search "edge-colorings sampling 2026 threshold" 2026-11-16 found near-2d algorithmic bounds, tree-specific improvements and simultaneous-coloring results, but no general-graph computational phase-transition constant.

title: Linear-degree hardness threshold for colorings of bipartite graphs
statement: Determine the approximate-counting threshold for proper q-colorings of bipartite graphs of maximum degree Δ. In particular, is there an absolute c>0 such that approximate counting is #BIS-hard when q<(c+o(1))Δ as Δ→∞, where #BIS denotes counting independent sets of a bipartite graph?
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)
open_check: Web search "bipartite colorings BIS linear hardness 2026" 2026-11-16 found existing #BIS-hardness results and triangle-free sampling algorithms, but no linear-in-Δ hardness threshold closing their gap.

title: Remove the parity restriction in hypergraph-coloring counting hardness
statement: For odd q≥3, establish a counterpart of the known NP-hardness of approximating the number of proper q-colorings of K-uniform hypergraphs at maximum degree of order q^(K/2). The source also proposes the weaker target Δ≥q^((1/2+o(1))K), allowing a small deterioration in the exponent as K grows.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)

title: FPRAS or hardness for the random-cluster model with cluster weight between one and two
statement: For fixed rational 1<q<2 and edge probability 0<p<1, determine whether Z_RC(G;p,q)=sum_{A⊆E} p^|A|(1−p)^(|E|−|A|)q^k(A) has an FPRAS on arbitrary finite graphs. Here k(A) is the number of connected components of (V,A); an alternative resolution is a conditional inapproximability theorem.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)
open_check: Web search "random cluster FPRAS noninteger q between 1 and 2 2025 2026" 2026-11-16 found q=2 algorithms and special-geometry random-cluster results but no unrestricted-graph classification for this interval. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.

title: Hard-core deterministic approximation with parameter-independent polynomial exponent
statement: For every fixed Δ≥3 and 0<λ<λ_c(Δ)=(Δ−1)^(Δ−1)/(Δ−2)^Δ, is there a deterministic relative-ε approximation to Z_G(λ) running in f(Δ,λ)(n/ε)^C time on all maximum-degree-Δ graphs, for a universal C independent of Δ and λ? The parameter-dependent factor f may be arbitrary but finite.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)
open_check: Web search "hardcore model deterministic FPTAS exponent independent maximum degree 2025 2026" 2026-11-16 found correlation-decay and zero-free-region algorithms, but no universal-exponent FPTAS throughout uniqueness.

title: Subquadratic hard-core counting throughout the uniqueness regime
statement: For each fixed Δ≥3 and λ<λ_c(Δ)=(Δ−1)^(Δ−1)/(Δ−2)^Δ, is there δ=δ(Δ,λ)>0 and an FPRAS with work Otilde_(Δ,λ)(n^(2−δ)/ε²) for Z_G(λ) on every maximum-degree-Δ graph? The target covers all strictly subcritical fugacities rather than only a smaller high-temperature interval.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)

title: Approximation complexity of counting bipartite independent sets
statement: Does the number of independent sets of an arbitrary bipartite graph admit an FPRAS, or can one establish conditional intractability? An FPRAS must give relative error ε with success probability at least 3/4 in time polynomial in the graph size and 1/ε.
source_title: NII Shonan Meeting Report No. 186: Markov Chain Monte Carlo 2.0 — Heng Guo and Yitong Yin, organizers (2023)
locator: Talk abstract “Uniqueness and Rapid Mixing in the Bipartite Hardcore Model”, p. 3

title: Stationary robustness controlled by ordinary mixing time
statement: For lazy random walk P on a graph of maximum degree d, a strong ε-adversary chooses at each step a kernel (1−ε)P+εB_t, where B_t may depend on the past and has support contained in that of P. For every α>0, does ε≤c_α/√(d t_mix) imply π_ε^+(S)≤C_α π(S)^(1−α) for every S, where π_ε^+(S) is the supremal long-run occupation frequency under such adversaries?
source_title: Markov Chain Robustness — David Zuckerman (ITCS 2026)
open_check: Web search "Markov Chain Robustness upper separation" 2026-11-16 found the theorem with upper-separation time t_up and no replacement by ordinary total-variation t_mix.
why_it_matters: It would control long-term sampling bias using the familiar mixing parameter alone.
computational: For small chains optimize adversarial transitions by Markov decision programming and compare extremal occupation frequencies.

title: Efficient approximation of cover-time robustness
statement: For a connected graph with random-walk kernel P, let t_cov^+(ε) be the largest expected cover time over starting states and history-dependent kernels P_t satisfying (1−ε)P_ij≤(P_t)_ij≤(1+ε)P_ij. Is ρ_cov(2)=sup{ε∈[0,1):t_cov^+(ε)≤2t_cov} computable up to universal constant factors in polynomial time from the graph?
source_title: Markov Chain Robustness — David Zuckerman (ITCS 2026)
open_check: Web search "Markov Chain Robustness computational" 2026-11-16 found no polynomial-time approximation theorem for cover-time robustness; the source explicitly asks efficient computability of its robustness parameters.

title: Hitting-time robustness of higher-dimensional grids
statement: For the nearest-neighbor random walk on G_L={1,…,L}^d with fixed d≥2, determine the asymptotic order of ρ_hit(2) as L→∞. Here t_hit^+(ε) is the maximum expected vertex-hitting time under all adaptive stochastic kernels P_t with entries in [(1−ε)P_ij,(1+ε)P_ij], and ρ_hit(2)=sup{ε:t_hit^+(ε)≤2t_hit}.
source_title: Markov Chain Robustness — David Zuckerman (ITCS 2026)
open_check: Web search "Markov Chain Robustness grid" 2026-11-16 found the source’s general bounds and solved path/expander cases, but no sharp higher-dimensional-grid robustness asymptotic.
why_it_matters: It measures how much local transition error a spatial sampler tolerates before its exploration slows substantially.
computational: Solve optimal hitting-control Bellman equations on small grids and fit the dependence on L for d=2,3.

title: Hitting-time robustness of the hypercube
statement: For random walk that flips one uniformly selected coordinate of {0,1}^d, determine the asymptotic order of ρ_hit(2) as d→∞. Define t_hit^+(ε) by maximizing expected vertex-hitting times over adaptive kernels whose entries differ multiplicatively from the original kernel by at most 1±ε, and set ρ_hit(2)=sup{ε:t_hit^+(ε)≤2t_hit}.
source_title: Markov Chain Robustness — David Zuckerman (ITCS 2026)
open_check: Web search "robustness hypercube Zuckerman" 2026-11-16 found no sharp hypercube hitting-robustness result; the source lists hypercubes among its unresolved graph families.
why_it_matters: The cube tests whether high dimension and many short routes protect sampling against small local bias.
computational: Exploit cube symmetries to reduce adversarial hitting-time optimization to Hamming-distance states for symmetric candidate policies.

title: One-logarithm mixing bound in terms of vertex conductance
statement: For a connected n-vertex graph G, let Ψ(G)=min_{0<|S|≤n/2}|{v∉S:v has a neighbor in S}|/|S|, and let τ*(G) be the infimum of t_mix(1/4) over lazy reversible kernels supported on G with uniform stationary law. Is τ*(G)≤C Ψ(G)^−2 log n for a universal C, improving the known log²n bound?
source_title: Geometric bounds on the fastest mixing Markov chain — Sam Olesker-Taylor and Luca Zanetti (2024)
open_check: Web search "fastest mixing log vertex conductance 2025 2026" 2026-11-16 found improved optimal-gap bounds but no general one-logarithm theorem for the fastest total-variation mixing time.
why_it_matters: It asks how closely a well-designed reversible walk can match the graph’s vertex expansion.
computational: Use semidefinite optimization to find fast symmetric kernels on small graphs and compare their mixing with Ψ(G).

title: Sharpness of the cubic dimension factor for coordinate hit-and-run
statement: For bounded convex K⊂R^n containing the Euclidean unit ball, let π be uniform on K and C_PI(π) its Poincaré constant. Determine whether the universal lower bound gap_CHAR≥c/(n³ C_PI(π)) for coordinate hit-and-run is asymptotically sharp, by constructing bodies with gap_CHAR=O(1/(n³ C_PI)) or improving the n³ factor.
source_title: Spectral Gaps of Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run — Yunbum Kook and Santosh S. Vempala (2026)
open_check: Web search "coordinate hit-and-run tight 2026" 2026-11-16 found the new cubic Poincaré bound and faster simplex-specific results, but no general matching lower construction or improved factor.
why_it_matters: It identifies the inherent penalty of restricting geometric sampling to coordinate directions.
computational: Discretize low-dimensional rotated and elongated convex polytopes and estimate coordinate-update spectral gaps.

title: Logarithmic correction to the two-dimensional FA-1f relaxation time
statement: On Z² let each site resample to vacant with probability q and occupied with probability 1−q at rate one, but only when at least one nearest neighbor is vacant. Prove that the inverse L² spectral gap in the Bernoulli equilibrium measure satisfies T_rel(q)=Θ(q^−2 log(1/q)) as q↓0; the missing part in the source is the logarithmic lower bound.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "FA-1f relaxation lower bound logarithm" 2026-11-16 found the known q^−2 to q^−2 log(1/q) gap and no matching logarithmic lower theorem; the 2025 book retains Conjecture 4.3.

computational: Diagonalize constrained generators on small periodic boxes and use variational trial functions based on vacancy clusters.

title: Sharp exponential relaxation scale for planar FA-2f
statement: For FA-2f on Z², each vertex has a rate-one clock and resamples a Bernoulli(1−q) occupation only if at least two nearest neighbors are vacant. Prove lim_{q↓0} q log T_rel(q)=π²/9 for the infinite-volume equilibrium inverse spectral gap, upgrading the sharp infection-time asymptotic to a relaxation-time asymptotic.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "FA-2f spectral gap 2026" 2026-11-16 found sharp infection-time and universality results but no proof of the book’s sharp relaxation-time conjecture.

title: One-dimensional unrooted constrained-dynamics infection exponent
statement: Let U be a finite family of finite subsets of Z\{0}, containing an update rule entirely in the positive half-line and one entirely in the negative half-line. A site resamples a Bernoulli(1−q) occupation at rate one when some translate x+U is all vacant; starting from equilibrium, let τ0 be the first vacancy time at the origin. Prove existence of and determine α(U)>0 such that lim_{C→∞} liminf_{q↓0} P(1/C≤q^α τ0≤C)=1.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "kinetically constrained unrooted one dimension scaling" 2026-11-16 found universality results in other settings but no complete determination of the source’s one-dimensional infection exponent.

title: Low-vacancy asymptotics of the East front speed
statement: In the one-dimensional East process, a site updates at rate one to vacancy probability q only when its right neighbor is vacant. Start with all sites left of the origin occupied and a vacancy at the origin, and let X_t be the leftmost vacancy. Determine the sharp q↓0 asymptotics of the deterministic positive speed v(q)=lim_{t→∞}(−X_t)/t.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "East model front velocity small q" 2026-11-16 found existence of a ballistic front and its invariant environment, but no sharp low-q speed asymptotic.
why_it_matters: The front speed sets the leading mixing scale for large finite East systems.
computational: Simulate the process in a moving frame and estimate v(q), using rare-event methods for small q.

title: Correlations in the stationary East environment seen from its front
statement: For the East process on Z with vacancy probability q and right-neighbor facilitation, let μtilde_q be the invariant law of the configuration seen from the leftmost vacancy, so the front is at coordinate 0. Quantify the adjacent-site covariances Cov_{μtilde_q}(η_i,η_{i+1}) for i≥1, including their q↓0 behavior and dependence on distance from the front.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "East front measure density 2026" 2026-11-16 found existence and far-behind-front convergence results but no quantitative adjacent-correlation description requested in Problem 7.13.
why_it_matters: The front environment controls propagation speeds and deviations from local equilibrium.

title: Exponential local equilibration after an ergodic KCM temperature quench
statement: For a finite update family U on Z^d, run rate-one constrained Bernoulli resampling with vacancy probability q>q_c(U), the ergodicity threshold, from an independent Bernoulli initial law of vacancy density q0>q_c(U). Prove that for every bounded local function f there are c,C>0 such that |E_{μ_q0} f(η_t)−μ_q(f)|≤C exp(−ct) for all t≥0.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "kinetically constrained cutoff 2026" 2026-11-16 found high-vacancy and oriented-model progress but no all-update-family exponential quench-equilibration theorem.
why_it_matters: It would extend equilibrium spectral information to physically natural nonequilibrium starts.
computational: Compare local-observable decay after Bernoulli quenches across oriented, isotropic and cooperative update rules.

title: Linear-time cutoff for general ergodic kinetically constrained models
statement: Fix a finite update family U on Z^d and vacancy probability q>q_c(U). For the constrained heat-bath chain in {1,…,n}^d with all exterior sites vacant and rate-one clocks at each interior site, prove that there is v(U,q)>0 such that t_mix(ε)/n→v(U,q) for every fixed 0<ε<1. Updates at x are allowed when x+U is vacant for at least one U in the update family.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "kinetically constrained cutoff 2026" 2026-11-16 found the September 2026 linear pre-cutoff result for oriented models, but no full general linear-time cutoff theorem.
why_it_matters: It would establish an abrupt and predictable equilibration time for an entire class of constrained Glauber dynamics.
computational: Simulate mixing from blocked-looking configurations on growing boxes and estimate whether the transition window is sublinear in n.

title: Local density after a KCM quench into the nonergodic phase
statement: Let U be a finite update family on Z^d with 0<q_c(U)<1. Start its constrained Bernoulli-resampling dynamics from product vacancy density q0>q_c(U), but evolve with q<q_c(U). Determine whether lim_{t→∞} E_{μ_q0}[η_0(t)]=1−q, and, when this fails or a limit does not exist, characterize the resulting local-density behavior.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "kinetically constrained temperature quench nonergodic local density" 2026-11-16 found no general Zd classification; the source poses the local-density question and warns that a tree analogue can fail. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.

computational: Simulate quenches for North-East and Spiral-type rules, tracking occupation density and the distribution of blocked-cluster sizes.

title: Diffusive equilibrium relaxation in Kob–Andersen lattice gases
statement: Consider the Kob–Andersen j-facilitated conservative particle process on Z^d, 2≤j≤d, at equilibrium vacancy density q∈(0,1). A particle may exchange with a vacant nearest neighbor only when both endpoint sites have at least j−1 additional vacant neighbors. Prove the diffusive estimate Var_{μ_q}(P_t f)=O_{f,q}(t^−d/2) for every bounded local f, improving the source’s general O(1/t) bound where d>2.
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "Kob-Andersen equilibrium relaxation decay" 2026-11-16 found finite-box diffusive gaps and tagged-particle results but no full infinite-volume diffusive local-relaxation theorem.
why_it_matters: It tests whether constrained conservative dynamics share the long-time universality of simple exclusion.
computational: Measure equilibrium autocorrelations in moderate periodic boxes and compare finite-size scaling with t^−d/2.

title: Sharp critical exponents for oriented all-children-facilitated tree dynamics
statement: On the rooted k-ary tree of depth L, fix the exterior children vacant and let each vertex resample a Bernoulli(p) occupation at rate one only when all k children are vacant. At p=1/k, are T_rel=Θ(L²) and t_mix(1/4)=Θ(L³) as L→∞? The source proves these lower orders and polynomially larger upper bounds.
source_title: Mixing time of a kinetically constrained spin model on trees: power law scaling at criticality — N. Cancrini, F. Martinelli, C. Roberto and C. Toninelli (2015)
open_check: Web search "kinetically constrained trees critical relaxation 2025 2026" 2026-11-16 found the polynomial-depth theorem but no matching critical exponents; §5 explicitly asks whether its lower exponents are correct.
why_it_matters: It would give exact critical slowdown for a tractable constrained analogue of tree Glauber dynamics.

title: Quasi-critical relaxation exponent for oriented facilitated tree dynamics
statement: On the infinite rooted k-ary tree, consider rate-one Bernoulli(p) resampling allowed only when all k children are vacant. As p↑p_c=1/k from below, determine the exact divergence exponent of the inverse equilibrium spectral gap; in particular is T_rel(p)=Θ((p_c−p)^−2), matching the known lower bound?
source_title: Mixing time of a kinetically constrained spin model on trees: power law scaling at criticality — N. Cancrini, F. Martinelli, C. Roberto and C. Toninelli (2015)
open_check: Web search "OFA critical relaxation" 2026-11-16 found the known (p_c−p)^−2 lower and polynomial upper bounds but no sharp quasi-critical exponent.
why_it_matters: It links the closing spectral gap to the percolation transition underlying the kinetic constraint.
computational: Estimate equilibrium persistence and spectral variational bounds near p_c on finite trees, controlling depth before extrapolation.

title: Polynomial critical relaxation at the discontinuous tree facilitation transition
statement: On a rooted ternary tree of depth L with vacant exterior children, each vertex resamples Bernoulli(p) at rate one when at least two of its three children are vacant. At the bootstrap critical occupation p_c=8/9, is the inverse spectral gap bounded by a polynomial in L, as conjectured, and what is its asymptotic order?
source_title: Mixing time of a kinetically constrained spin model on trees: power law scaling at criticality — N. Cancrini, F. Martinelli, C. Roberto and C. Toninelli (2015)
open_check: Web search "oriented facilitated 8/9 relaxation" 2026-11-16 found the source’s polynomial-relaxation conjecture and no proof or counterexample at this discontinuous critical point.
why_it_matters: It distinguishes the dynamics of continuous and discontinuous kinetic transitions.

title: Aldous’s n-to-the-three-halves triangulation relaxation conjecture
statement: On triangulations of a convex (n+2)-gon, select an internal diagonal uniformly and, with probability 1/2, replace it by the opposite diagonal of its adjacent quadrilateral. Prove that the inverse spectral gap of this lazy uniform-triangulation chain is Θ(n^(3/2)); the 2026 source gives an Otilde(n²) upper bound.
source_title: Faster Triangulation Mixing via Transport Flows — Vedat Levi Alev, Daniel Frishberg, Michail Sarantis and Prasad Tetali (2026)

computational: Enumerate Catalan-many triangulations through n≈10 and compute gaps; compare with variational bottleneck constructions.

title: Mixing of the double-flip chain on disjoint triangulation pairs
statement: Let the state be an ordered pair (T1,T2) of triangulations of a convex n-gon with no common internal diagonal. At each step choose uniformly among the 2(n−3) diagonals in the pair, flip it in its triangulation, and, if the new diagonal occurs in the other triangulation, flip that copy too. Determine the asymptotic total-variation mixing time of the resulting uniform-stationary chain as n→∞.
source_title: Sampling planar tanglegrams and pairs of disjoint triangulations — Alexander Black, Kevin Liu, Alex McDonough, Garrett Nelson, Michael Wigal, Mei Yin and Youngho Yoo (2023)
open_check: Web search "disjoint triangulations mixing 2026" 2026-11-16 found the connected regular-chain construction but no polynomial or sharp mixing analysis for disjoint pairs.
why_it_matters: It would yield an efficient sampler for irreducible planar tanglegrams.
computational: Enumerate the flip graph for n≤9 (46,782 states at n=9 in the source) and estimate gaps and mixing curves.

title: Sharp first-order oracle complexity of strongly log-concave sampling
statement: For C² potentials V:R^d→R satisfying I≼∇²V≼κI and with a known minimizer, determine the minimax number of adaptive exact queries (V(x),∇V(x)) needed to output a law within ε of π∝e^(−V) in total variation. In particular, close the remaining dimension-dependent gap at κ=2 and fixed ε∈(0,1/10), where the 2026 source gives a superpolylogarithmic lower bound and cites subpolynomial upper bounds.
source_title: Towards the Query Complexity of Sampling under Strong Log-Concavity and Log-Sobolev Inequalities — Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki (2026)
open_check: Web searches "log-concave sampling query complexity 2026 optimal" and "2611.05813" 2026-11-16 found September subpolynomial upper bounds and November superpolylogarithmic lower bounds, with the exact joint complexity still open in §9.
why_it_matters: It would establish the intrinsic cost of smooth convex sampling beyond the Gaussian case.

title: Sharp oracle complexity of sampling under a log-Sobolev inequality
statement: For integrable densities π∝e^(−V) on R^d with L-Lipschitz gradient and log-Sobolev inequality Ent_π(f²)≤(2/α)∫|∇f|²dπ, determine the minimax exact first-order-query complexity for ε-total-variation sampling as a function of d, κ=L/α and ε. Work in the warm-start model where one sample X0 from an unknown density ν with dν/dπ≤M is supplied for fixed M; the source’s Ω(κ) lower bound holds even in this model.
source_title: Towards the Query Complexity of Sampling under Strong Log-Concavity and Log-Sobolev Inequalities — Huanjian Zhou and Taiji Suzuki (2026)
open_check: Web search "log-Sobolev sampling query complexity 2611.05813" 2026-11-16 found the November Ω(κ) lower bound but no matching joint dimension-condition-accuracy theorem; §9 leaves that dependence open.
why_it_matters: It measures the extra sampling cost of allowing nonconvex potentials with good functional inequalities.
computational: Numerically test hidden-cap potentials and estimate their functional inequalities and oracle distinguishability; general lower bounds require proof.

title: Two-batch counting-to-sampling reduction with optimal annealing work
statement: Let Z(β)=Σ_x F(x)e^(βH(x)) for finite Ω, known nonnegative F and H(Ω)⊂{0}∪[1,h], and suppose independent samples from π_β are available at any β in a prescribed interval. Given q≥log(Z(β_max)/Z(β_min)), can one estimate that ratio to relative error ε with probability at least 0.7 using O(q log h/ε²) samples in only two total batches, each batch’s temperatures chosen before its samples are observed? The source obtains this work in three total batches.
source_title: Near-Optimal Parallel Approximate Counting via Sampling — David G. Harris, Vladimir Kolmogorov, Hongyang Liu, Yitong Yin and Yiyao Zhang (2026)
open_check: Web search "two-round partition functions sampling 2026" 2026-11-16 found the three-batch theorem (two rounds of adaptivity plus estimation), but no two-total-batch algorithm with the same work.
why_it_matters: It would remove a remaining sequential barrier in converting sampling into approximate counting.
computational: Search small finite Hamiltonians for lower-bound pairs with nearly identical first-batch observations; prototype schedules on two-level and multilevel systems.

title: Total-variation cutoff for Kac’s walk on SO(n)
statement: At each discrete step choose a coordinate pair uniformly from the n(n−1)/2 possibilities and an independent uniform angle in [0,2π), then multiply the current matrix by that plane rotation. Does this walk, started at the identity and targeting Haar measure on SO(n), have total-variation cutoff as n→∞, meaning t_mix(ε)/t_mix(1−ε)→1 for every fixed ε∈(0,1/2)? The September 2026 preprint claims quadratic-scale pre-cutoff but explicitly leaves cutoff undecided.
source_title: Resolvent characteristics and quadratic mixing of Kac’s walk on SO(n) — Yunjiang Jiang (2026)
open_check: Web search "Kac cutoff 2609.08018" 2026-11-16 found the September quadratic pre-cutoff claim, whose abstract explicitly establishes neither presence nor absence of cutoff, and no subsequent resolution.
why_it_matters: It asks whether a basic high-dimensional rotation sampler equilibrates in a sharp window.
computational: Simulate plane rotations for increasing n and compare several observables and multiscale distance proxies; these alone cannot certify total variation.

title: Rapid mixing of Chodrow’s hypergraph edge-repartition chain
statement: On simple r-uniform hypergraphs with a prescribed vertex-degree sequence, choose two hyperedges e,f uniformly and replace them by uniformly chosen e′,f′ preserving all vertex degrees and the intersection e∩f; reject nonsimple outcomes and add laziness. Determine broad classes of degree sequences and r for which the chain’s total-variation mixing time is polynomial in the input size and log(1/ε). The source establishes the question after discussing ergodicity.
source_title: Generating graphs randomly — Catherine Greenhill (2021; arXiv version updated 2025)
open_check: Web search "Chodrow mixing 2026 hypergraphs" 2026-11-16 found new hypergraph samplers and empirical comparisons but no general polynomial mixing theorem for this edge-repartition chain.
why_it_matters: It would support rigorous sampling of hypergraphs with fixed degrees rather than relying on empirical burn-in.
computational: Enumerate the state graphs for small r and degree sequences and compute exact gaps or conductance bottlenecks.

title: Sharp mixing and cutoff for the card-weighted adhesive riffle shuffle
statement: Fix p∈(0,1). Cut an n-card deck at K∼Bin(n,1/2) and independently retain each internal contact within each packet with probability p, forming intact ordered blocks. With A and B cards remaining in the two packets, choose the next packet with probabilities A/(A+B) and B/(A+B), and emit its entire leading block. Determine the asymptotic total-variation mixing time to uniform on S_n and whether cutoff occurs as n→∞.
source_title: Adhesive riffle shuffles: one-parameter models and mixing bounds — Yunjiang Jiang (2026)
open_check: Web search "adhesive shuffles mixing Jiang cutoff 2026" 2026-11-16 found the November source’s nonmatching fixed-p bounds and no later sharp mixing or cutoff theorem for this specified release rule.
why_it_matters: It tests how correlated blocks change the classical riffle-shuffle mixing transition.
computational: Construct transition matrices for n≤8 and simulate larger decks over fixed p values; estimate spectral gaps and compare distance curves.

title: Sharp mixing scale of unglued even-deck midpoint interpolation
statement: For even n, cut a deck at K∼Bin(n,1/2), give card j of each nonempty m-card packet key (j−1/2)/m, and interleave by increasing keys with independent fair coins for cross-packet ties. Determine the total-variation mixing order to uniform as n→∞ through even values, and whether it has cutoff. The source proves Ω(√n log n) and O(n^(5/2) log n), leaving a factor n² between the scales.
source_title: Adhesive riffle shuffles: one-parameter models and mixing bounds — Yunjiang Jiang (2026)
open_check: Web search "adhesive shuffles mixing Jiang cutoff 2026" 2026-11-16 found only the source’s Ω(√n log n)–O(n^(5/2) log n) gap for unglued even-deck interpolation and no sharp-scale result.
why_it_matters: It isolates the amount of randomness produced by tied deterministic interpolation schedules.
computational: Compute exact matrices through small even n and track the √n log n scaling against polynomial alternatives in simulations.

title: Degree-two spectral-gap reduction for Brownian energy diffusion
statement: Let η lie in {η∈R^n_+:Ση_i=1}, with Dirichlet(α_1,…,α_n) equilibrium, α_i>0, and connected nonnegative edge weights w_ij. For the Brownian energy generator Lf=Σ_{i<j}w_ij[η_iη_j(∂_i−∂_j)²f+(α_iη_j−α_jη_i)(∂_i−∂_j)f], is the spectral gap always attained by a polynomial in η of degree at most two?
source_title: Aldous’ spectral gap phenomena in stochastic exchange models — Pietro Caputo, Matteo Quattropani and Federico Sau (2026)
open_check: Web search "Brownian energy process degree two spectral gap 2026" 2026-11-16 found the October SIP/BEP paper’s small-diffusivity reduction but no all-parameter proof; the September source explicitly leaves the general case open.
why_it_matters: It would reduce an infinite-dimensional variational problem to a quadratic-size matrix.
computational: Compute the generator on polynomial layers through degree six for small weighted graphs, using rational α and exact arithmetic.

title: Aldous–Caputo spectral-gap conjecture on the unitary group
statement: For a connected weighted hypergraph Γ on [n], let a continuous-time walk on U(n) independently replace the coordinate submatrix on B by left multiplication with a Haar-random U(B), at rate w_B. Is its spectral gap the minimum of the smallest generator eigenvalues in the two irreducible representations of highest weights (1,0,…,0,−1) and (2,0,…,0,−2)? Equivalently, is it exactly the gap of the two-particle discrete KMP process that uniformly redistributes particles inside the selected hyperedge?
source_title: Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups — Gil Alon and Doron Puder (2026)
open_check: Web search "Aldous-type Spectral Gaps unitary solved" 2026-11-16 found partial unitary results; Caputo–Quattropani–Sau 2609.10450 solves the particle-only KMP conjecture but explicitly leaves the full unitary conjecture open.
why_it_matters: It would identify a universal low-degree obstruction to mixing for local random unitary updates.
computational: Compute low-weight representation matrices for n=3,4 and rational hyperedge rates to search for violations of the proposed ordering.

title: Stronger unitary representation domination outside the exceptional quadratic mode
statement: For a weighted hypergraph Γ, define L_ρ=Σ_B w_B(I−∫_{U(B)}ρ(g)dg) on an irreducible U(n)-representation ρ. Is λ_min(L_(1,0,…,0,−1))≤λ_min(L_ρ) for every nontrivial ρ other than highest weight (2,0,…,0,−2)? The question is stronger than identifying the overall unitary gap and would imply the hypergraph interchange-gap conjecture via the source’s comparison theorem.
source_title: Aldous-type Spectral Gaps in Unitary Groups — Gil Alon and Doron Puder (2026)
open_check: Web search "Aldous U(n) conjecture 2026" 2026-11-16 found the source and the subsequent KMP degree-two theorem, but no resolution of this stronger representation-by-representation domination question.
why_it_matters: It would explain which modes can slow random unitary walks and connect them to permutation-chain gaps.
computational: Enumerate highest weights of bounded total size for n≤4 and compare the eigenvalues of their Haar-averaging projection sums.

title: Exact modified log-Sobolev constant of the complete graph
statement: For the continuous-time walk on n≥3 vertices with jump rate one to every other vertex and uniform law π, determine exactly ρ_n=inf_{f>0,Ent_π(f)>0} E(f,log f)/Ent_π(f), where E(f,log f)=(1/(2n))Σ_{i,j}(f_i−f_j)(log f_i−log f_j). Here Ent_π(f)=n^−1Σ_i f_i log f_i−f̄ log f̄ and f̄=n^−1Σ_i f_i. The source only bounds n≤ρ_n≤2n.
source_title: Entropy inequalities for random walks and permutations — Alexandre Bristiel and Pietro Caputo (2024)
open_check: Web search "complete graph modified log-Sobolev exact 2026" 2026-11-16 found exact ordinary log-Sobolev constants and modified inequalities up to constants, but no explicit value for this n-state modified constant.
why_it_matters: It is a basic unresolved sharp entropy-contraction constant even for the simplest nontrivial reversible kernel.
computational: Reduce the variational search to candidate f with two distinct coordinate values, then solve the one-variable stationary equations with certified interval arithmetic.
status_note: Not open. Y. Gu and Y. Polyanskiy, Non-linear log-Sobolev inequalities for the Potts semigroup, arXiv:2005.05444 (2020), Comm. Math. Phys. 404 (2023) 769-831: Theorem 1 with (10) at p=1 gives rho(K_n)=n(1+inf D(1/n||s)/D(s||1/n)) with one-vertex minimisers; Proposition 2 gives n+n/log n <= rho <= n+(1+o(1))n/log n. Bristiel-Caputo Remark 1.2 (2021) overlooks it. Found by the first-reader audit 16 Nov 2026.

title: One-dimensional Fisher-information sampling complexity
statement: Let π∝e^(−V) on R have 1-Lipschitz derivative, with no convexity or functional inequality assumed. Given exact queries (V(x),V′(x)) and initialization from a law ρ0 with KL(ρ0‖π)≤1, determine the optimal worst-case query dependence on ε for output law ρ satisfying ∫|(log(dρ/dπ))′|²dρ≤ε². The source leaves a gap between its roughly ε^−2 upper bound and the one-dimensional lower bound from earlier work.
source_title: Complexity of Non-Log-Concave Sampling in Fisher Information — Sinho Chewi and Andre Wibisono (2026)
open_check: Web search "Fisher information dimension one sampling 2026 complexity" 2026-11-16 found the May 2026 paper and no later matching one-dimensional bound; its conclusion explicitly leaves this case open.
why_it_matters: It tests whether approximate stationarity can be substantially cheaper in low-dimensional sampling.
computational: Optimize one-dimensional bump-potential adversaries and simulate proximal samplers with numerical quadrature to examine candidate ε exponents.

title: Constant-time WSK mixing for three-colourings of the even square torus
statement: On the N×N nearest-neighbour torus with even N, consider the uniform law on proper three-colourings. A WSK step chooses an unordered colour pair uniformly and independently swaps the two colours on each connected component of the subgraph they induce with probability 1/2. Is the worst-start total-variation mixing time t_mix(1/4)=O(1) uniformly as N→∞?
source_title: Approximate Colorwise Tensorization of Entropy and Optimal Mixing of the Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký Dynamics — Chunyang Wang, Yuichi Yoshida and Zihan Zhang (2026)
open_check: Web search "WSK mixing 2026 torus" 2026-11-16 found numerical support and the July entropy-tensorization paper but no constant-time mixing theorem for critical three-colourings of this torus.
why_it_matters: It would rigorously capture the proposed absence of critical slowing down for a cluster sampler.
computational: Enumerate proper colourings on tiny even tori, build the WSK kernel, and compare gap and observable-autocorrelation scaling in larger simulations.

title: Rapid WSK mixing for general edge colourings down to Δ+2 colours
statement: For every graph G with maximum degree Δ and q≥Δ+2, consider WSK on its proper q-edge-colourings: choose two colours and independently swap them on each connected component of the corresponding two-colour subgraph of the line graph. Is this chain rapidly mixing, with t_mix(ε) polynomial in |E(G)|, q and log(1/ε), throughout this known irreducibility regime?
source_title: Approximate Colorwise Tensorization of Entropy and Optimal Mixing of the Wang–Swendsen–Kotecký Dynamics — Chunyang Wang, Yuichi Yoshida and Zihan Zhang (2026)
open_check: Web search "WSK edge colorings rapid mixing" 2026-11-16 found the July 2026 tree results and general irreducibility at q≥Δ+2, but no polynomial mixing theorem on all graphs in that regime. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It would give an efficient cluster sampler in a range where single-edge updates can be disconnected.
computational: Enumerate Kempe-equivalence state graphs for small Δ-regular graphs and search for exponentially small conductance.

title: Cutoff at the upper dynamical threshold for mean-field Swendsen–Wang
statement: Fix an integer q≥3 and the q-state Potts law on K_n proportional to exp((β/n)Σ_{i<j}1{σ_i=σ_j}), at β=q. Each Swendsen–Wang step retains monochromatic edges independently with probability 1−e^(−β/n), then assigns every resulting component an independent uniform colour. Determine whether worst-start total-variation cutoff occurs as n→∞, namely t_mix(ε)/t_mix(1−ε)→1 for each fixed ε∈(0,1/2).
source_title: Cutoff for the Swendsen–Wang Dynamics on the Complete Graph — Antonio Blanca and Zongchen Song (2025)
open_check: Web search "Swendsen cutoff critical 2026" 2026-11-16 found cutoff strictly above β=q and the 2025 source explicitly leaving the dynamical endpoints open, with no endpoint resolution located. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It tests sharp mixing at the boundary of the mean-field metastability window.
computational: Simulate the finite-dimensional colour-count chain and estimate first-passage fluctuations around the dynamical bottleneck.

title: Uniform chance of meeting before either walk hits a stationary target
statement: Let X,Y be independent copies of an irreducible finite continuous-time reversible chain, both started from stationarity π, and let Z independently have law π. Write M=inf{t≥0:X_t=Y_t}, H_X=inf{t≥0:X_t=Z}, and H_Y similarly. Is there a universal ε>0 such that P(M≤min(H_X,H_Y))≥ε for every such chain?
source_title: How to create an open problem — Louigi Addario-Berry (2022)
open_check: Web search "Addario-Berry meeting sitting duck" 2026-11-16 found the 2022 problem note but no proof or counterexample to this universal positive meeting-before-target probability.
why_it_matters: It would compare coalescence with coverage in a way that does not require geometric assumptions on the chain.
computational: For small rational reversible kernels, solve the absorbing product-chain equations on triples and minimize the probability over conductances.

title: Deterministic FPTAS for the nonnegative permanent
statement: Given an n×n matrix A of nonnegative rational entries and ε∈(0,1), is there a deterministic algorithm running in time polynomial in the bit length of A and ε^−1 that outputs Z with (1−ε)per(A)≤Z≤(1+ε)per(A)? Here per(A)=Σ_{σ∈S_n}∏_i A_{i,σ(i)}, so the same question concerns weighted bipartite perfect-matching counting.
source_title: Subexponential Approximation of the Permanent in Deterministic Polynomial Time — Sergei Kudria, Jason Luo and Mahbod Majid (2026)
open_check: Web search "deterministic permanent open problem 2026" 2026-11-16 found September subexponential-factor and (1+ε)^n approximation algorithms, both explicitly leaving a fully polynomial deterministic relative scheme open.
why_it_matters: It would derandomize a central example of MCMC-based approximate counting.
computational: Compare deterministic scaling bounds with exact subset-DP permanent values for n≤22 to design and test sharper certificates.

title: Cutoff for the full upper-triangular matrix walk over F2
statement: On upper-triangular n×n matrices over F2 with every diagonal entry one, choose i uniformly from {1,…,n−1} and with probability 1/2 add row i+1 to row i. Does the resulting lazy walk, with uniform stationary law, have total-variation cutoff as n→∞? Cutoff for each fixed number of columns does not settle the question for the whole matrix.
source_title: Markov Chains and Mixing Times, second edition — David Levin and Yuval Peres, with Elizabeth Wilmer (2017)
open_check: Web searches "upper triangular cutoff walk mixing matrices" and "Gaussian elimination chain cutoff" 2026-11-16 found finite-column cutoff and cutoff for different random-generator or conjugacy-invariant walks, but no cutoff theorem for the full adjacent-row walk.
why_it_matters: It asks whether the East-model mixing front controls an entire nilpotent-group sampler.
computational: Enumerate the 2^(n(n−1)/2) states for n≤6 and simulate the full matrix and column projections for larger n.

title: Overlapping-cycles shuffle within a logarithm of one-card relaxation
statement: At each step on n cards, move either card n or card n−k to the top, independently with probability 1/2, retaining other relative orders, where 1≤k≤n−2. For a lazy version of both the full shuffle and its one-card projection, is t_mix(1/4)≤C log(n)/gap_one(n,k) uniformly over n,k? Here gap_one is one minus the largest modulus of a nontrivial one-card eigenvalue, and C is universal.
source_title: Card shuffling and Diophantine approximation — Omer Angel, Yuval Peres and David B. Wilson (2008)
open_check: Web search "overlapping-cycles shuffle mixing time Angel Peres Wilson solved" 2026-11-16 found Blumberg–Morris–Oberschelp 2310.15438 giving a log³ n overhead for major parameter regimes, but no uniform log n overhead.
why_it_matters: It would show that the slow motion of one card predicts the full nonreversible shuffle to logarithmic precision.
computational: Build n×n one-card kernels for many n,k and compare their eigenvalues with full permutation-chain mixing for n≤8.

title: Sharp uniform Diophantine upper envelope for the overlapping-cycles one-card gap
statement: For the nonlazy overlapping-cycles shuffle moving card n or n−k to the top equiprobably, let gap(n,k)=1−max{|λ|:λ is a nontrivial eigenvalue of its n-state one-card position kernel}. Is gap(n,k)≤(2π²/√3+o(1))√k/n² uniformly for 1≤k<n as n→∞? The source observes candidate k attaining this envelope at macroscopic k/n.
source_title: Card shuffling and Diophantine approximation — Omer Angel, Yuval Peres and David B. Wilson (2008)
open_check: Web search "overlapping-cycles spectral gap inequality" 2026-11-16 found the original single-card analysis and later full-deck mixing work, but no proof of the proposed sharp uniform envelope.
why_it_matters: It asks for the optimal spectral speed obtainable by choosing the two overlapping cycles.
computational: Compute roots of the explicit one-card characteristic polynomials with interval bounds for n up to several thousand and locate near-extremal k.

title: FPRAS for counting list packings with 2Δ colours per list
statement: Given a graph of maximum degree Δ and a list L(v) of exactly q≥2Δ colours at each vertex, a labelled list packing is a tuple (c_1,…,c_q) of proper list colourings such that {c_1(v),…,c_q(v)}=L(v) for every v. For each fixed Δ,q in this range, does the number of these packings admit a randomized relative ε approximation in time polynomial in the input size and ε^−1, with success probability at least 3/4?
source_title: Sampling List Packings — Evan Camrud, Ewan Davies, Alex Karduna and Holden Lee (2025)
open_check: Web search "list packings FPRAS 2026" 2026-11-16 found the ITCS 2025 Ω(Δ²)-list-size algorithm and no theorem reaching the conjectured q≥2Δ range. 2026-11-16: quote found in the source on a second fetch.
why_it_matters: It would extend efficient sampling and counting to a spin system with q! local states near its existence threshold.
computational: Enumerate packings on small graphs and examine the heat-bath and multi-vertex flip graphs for bottlenecks.

title: Efficient perfect sampling of list packings
statement: For lists L(v) of size q on an n-vertex graph of maximum degree Δ, output exactly uniformly a tuple of q proper list colourings that uses every entry of L(v) once at each vertex. Can this be done in expected time polynomial in the input size and q when q≥CΔ² for a universal sufficiently large C, the range where the source proves efficient approximate sampling?
source_title: Sampling List Packings — Evan Camrud, Ewan Davies, Alex Karduna and Holden Lee (2025)
open_check: Web search "list packings perfect sampling" 2026-11-16 found the source’s approximate heat-bath sampler and its suggestion of perfect sampling, but no expected-polynomial exact uniform algorithm for the stated range.
why_it_matters: It would eliminate burn-in and approximation error for the first algorithmic list-packing models.
computational: Develop a bounding-chain coupling from the past and exhaustively check its bounds against all q! local permutations for small q.

title: Spectral independence of proper colourings at Δ+2 colours
statement: For each fixed Δ and q≥Δ+2, is the uniform law on proper q-colourings of every graph of maximum degree Δ spectrally independent with a bound C(Δ,q) independent of the vertex count? Explicitly, after every feasible pinning, form the covariance matrix Σ of the remaining colour indicators and D with entries equal to their marginal probabilities, deleting zero-probability indicators; require λ_max(D^−1/2ΣD^−1/2)≤C(Δ,q).
source_title: Spectral Independence and Applications to Analysis of Markov Chains — Kuikui Liu, in Oberwolfach Report 27/2024 (2024)
open_check: Web search "spectral independence Δ+2 2026" 2026-11-16 found partial graph-class and larger-colour results but no all-graph Δ+2 theorem; the fetched 2024 report states this conjecture.
why_it_matters: It would bring a general local-to-global mixing method close to the natural colouring threshold.
computational: Enumerate pinned colouring distributions of small Δ-bounded graphs and compute the normalized covariance spectra exactly.

title: Equality of ergodicity and positive-gap thresholds for general KCM
statement: Let U be a finite family of finite subsets of Z^d\{0}; at each site resample a vacancy of density q at rate one when all sites in some translate x+X, X∈U, are vacant. Under equilibrium Bernoulli(q), let q_c be the infimum q for which the origin eventually becomes vacant almost surely and let q_gap be the infimum q for which the equilibrium spectral gap is positive. Is q_c=q_gap for every U and d?
source_title: Kinetically constrained models — Ivailo Hartarsky and Cristina Toninelli (2025)
open_check: Web search "bootstrap percolation sharp phase transition 2026 general" 2026-11-16 found sharpness for special update families but no all-family theorem; the source identifies this equality with its unresolved bootstrap sharpness conjecture.
why_it_matters: It would characterize exactly when an ergodic constrained dynamics has exponential equilibrium relaxation.
computational: For finite update families of small radius, enumerate bootstrap-stable sets and estimate finite-volume gap decay on increasing boxes.

title: Sharp exponential constant in moment-bounded nonconvex sampling complexity
statement: Consider all π∝e^(−V) on R^d with L-Lipschitz gradient, E_π|X|²≤M and a supplied stationary point ∇V(0)=0. Determine the infimum c>0 such that exact value-and-gradient oracle queries suffice for ε-total-variation sampling within (aLM/(dε))^(cd) queries for some universal a, in the regime LM≥d and LM/(dε)→∞. The source conjectures c=1/2.
source_title: On the query complexity of sampling from non-log-concave distributions — Yuchen He and Chihao Zhang (2025)
open_check: Web search "log-smooth second moment constant 2026 query complexity" 2026-11-16 found the He–Zhang exponential upper/lower bounds but no sharp exponent constant; §7 conjectures 1/2.
why_it_matters: It would refine the general information-theoretic cost of sampling without isoperimetry.
computational: Optimize hidden-well packings and truncation-based samplers in small dimensions to compare exponential constants.

title: Optimal weak Poincaré profiles from smoothness and a second-moment bound
statement: For π∝e^(−V) on R^d with L-Lipschitz gradient and E_π|X|²≤M, determine sharp uniform weak Poincaré bounds in d,L,M and r∈(0,1/4). Concretely, find the smallest worst-case B(d,L,M,r) such that Var_π(f)≤B∫|∇f|²dπ+r(sup f−inf f)² holds for all bounded smooth f and all targets in this class. This makes precise the source’s request for tight functional inequalities.
source_title: On the query complexity of sampling from non-log-concave distributions — Yuchen He and Chihao Zhang (2025)
open_check: Web search "log-smooth second moment constant 2026 query complexity" 2026-11-16 found oracle bounds using truncation but no tight uniform functional-inequality profile under just these assumptions; §7 asks for such inequalities.
why_it_matters: It would turn weak tail control into quantitative convergence guarantees without assuming a spectral gap.
computational: Optimize one-dimensional barrier potentials under moment and curvature constraints and compute discretized weak-Poincaré variational ratios.

title: When do hidden Gaussian mixtures admit subexponential oracle sampling?
statement: Suppose a target on R^d is a mixture of k nonsingular Gaussians, accessible only through exact values of its negative log-density and gradient, with L-Lipschitz log-gradient and second moment at most M. Characterize parameter regimes and structural conditions on these mixtures for which ε-total-variation sampling has exp(o(d)) query complexity as d→∞. The mixture weights, means and covariance matrices are not supplied to the sampler.
source_title: On the query complexity of sampling from non-log-concave distributions — Yuchen He and Chihao Zhang (2025)
open_check: Web search "query complexity 2502.06200 sharp" 2026-11-16 found the source and general moment-bounded lower bounds but no characterization of subexponential Gaussian-mixture oracle sampling; Problem 4 remains stated open.
why_it_matters: It separates tractable multimodal sampling from hidden-mode information barriers.
computational: Generate mixtures with hidden small-weight modes and vary separation, covariance anisotropy and k to test how quickly oracle queries reveal missing mass.

title: Half-fractional log-concavity of fixed-size matching vertex distributions
statement: Given a graph G and integer k with at least one k-edge matching, put μ(S) proportional to the number of perfect matchings of G[S] for each 2k-vertex subset S. Is z↦log(Σ_{|S|=2k}μ(S)∏_{i∈S}√z_i) concave on the positive orthant for every G,k? The source proves the analogous assertion with fourth roots and conjectures square roots.
source_title: Geometry-Inspired Sampling Algorithms and Random Graphs — Elizabeth Yang (2023)
open_check: Web search "fractionally log-concave matchings 1/2" 2026-11-16 found quarter-fractional results and the thesis’s half-fractional conjecture, but no proof or counterexample for all inputs.
why_it_matters: It would sharpen the local-to-global mixing guarantees for structured fixed-size samplers.
computational: For small graphs or rational matrices, compute the Hessian after the square-root substitution and seek a positive eigenvalue certificate.

title: Half-fractional log-concavity of nonsymmetric fixed-size DPPs
statement: Let L be a real n×n matrix with L+Lᵀ positive semidefinite, and assume Σ_{|S|=k}det(L_{S,S})>0. For μ(S) proportional to det(L_{S,S}) on k-subsets, is z↦log(Σ_{|S|=k}μ(S)∏_{i∈S}√z_i) concave on the positive orthant? The known quarter-fractional result replaces each square root by a fourth root.
source_title: Geometry-Inspired Sampling Algorithms and Random Graphs — Elizabeth Yang (2023)
open_check: Web search "nonsymmetric half log-concave DPP" 2026-11-16 found quarter-fractional results and the thesis’s half-fractional conjecture, but no proof or counterexample for all inputs.
why_it_matters: It would sharpen the local-to-global mixing guarantees for structured fixed-size samplers.
computational: For small graphs or rational matrices, compute the Hessian after the square-root substitution and seek a positive eigenvalue certificate.

title: Higher-marginal domain sparsification for fractional log-concavity
statement: Let μ be a law on k-subsets of [n] with generating polynomial g such that z↦log g(z_1^α,…,z_n^α) is concave, for fixed α>0. Given estimates and sample access for its inclusion marginals of order ℓ comparable to 1/α, can the domain-sparsification method be improved to use ground subsets T of size O(poly(k)polylog(n))? Here a sparsification method uses those marginals to select T, calls a sampler for the normalized restriction μ|T, and combines such calls to approximate μ within total-variation error 1/10, with overhead polynomial in k and log n after preprocessing. The source specifically asks this for α=1/2 and pairwise marginals.
source_title: Geometry-Inspired Sampling Algorithms and Random Graphs — Elizabeth Yang (2023)
open_check: Web search "domain sparsification higher-order marginals" 2026-11-16 found the conjecture and lower bounds for the weaker entropic-independence class, but no scheme achieving the proposed size for all fractionally log-concave laws.
why_it_matters: It would amortize repeated sampling by removing almost all dependence on the original domain size.
computational: Test sparsification schemes on matching and nonsymmetric-DPP laws with exact low-order marginals and exhaustive small-domain target comparisons.
